state_program_name: Home Care Organization (HCO) — licensed by CDSS Home Care Services Branch under the Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act (HSC §1796.10 et seq.); non-medical home care by registered home care aides

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose of This Manual

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** (the "Agency"), a Home Care Organization (HCO) licensed in California by the California Department of Social Services (CDSS), Home Care Services Branch, carries out its operations. The Agency provides **non-medical home care services** through employed, registry-listed affiliated home care aides, under the Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act (HSC §1796.10 et seq.).

The manual is intended to:

- Turn the licensing and operating requirements that apply to an HCO into clear, repeatable procedures for staff.
- Keep Agency practice consistent with the scope of "home care services" under HSC §1796.12. Those services are non-medical, and aides may not assist with medication that would otherwise require administration or oversight by a licensed health care professional.
- Support the content CDSS asks for in an HCO license application (CDSS HCS 281): personnel policies, a training plan, job descriptions, and a program description.
- Give owners, managers, aides, and office staff one reference for their duties, including mandated abuse reporting, background and TB clearance, training, insurance and bonding, and cooperation with CDSS inspections.
- Show inspectors, clients, and funding partners that the Agency operates under written, adopted policies.

**This manual is a template and must be customized.** Every `[AGENCY NAME]` placeholder and every other bracketed field must be replaced with Agency-specific information. Procedures must also be adjusted to the Agency's actual services, service area, hours, client population, funding sources, and organizational structure. A manual that has not been customized does not describe the Agency's practice.

**This manual is not legal advice.** Have qualified California counsel or a compliance professional review the customized manual before adoption.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

### 1. Customize it
- Replace all `[AGENCY NAME]` placeholders and bracketed fields with accurate Agency information (legal name, license number, designee, addresses, business hours, service area, contacts).
- Delete or revise any policy that does not match what the Agency does. For example, remove transportation or Medi-Cal-funded service provisions if the Agency does not offer them.
- Where this manual states an *agency policy choice* rather than a legal requirement (for example staffing practices, client-rights and grievance procedures, records-retention periods, or emergency planning), make sure it is labeled as Agency policy. The statutory sections reviewed for this manual do not set staffing ratios, client-rights or grievance rules, a records-retention period, or an emergency-plan rule. If the Agency adopts such policies, they are its own commitments, and the Agency must then follow them.
- Confirm items flagged for counsel. One is whether a pre-service dementia training component is required under the 2027 amendments to HSC §1796.44.

### 2. Adopt it
- The Agency's **governing body** (owner, board of directors, or managers of the LLC or corporation, as applicable) must formally review and adopt the customized manual. Record the adoption date, version, and approver in the manual's revision log.
- Corporations and LLCs should keep the board resolution on file. CDSS also requires a board resolution for the HCS 308 designee, and a licensee cannot designate itself.

### 3. Keep it current
- Review the manual on a set schedule (at least annually is recommended as Agency practice) and whenever laws, regulations, CDSS instructions, funding-program rules, or Agency operations change.
- Several provisions have dates that matter. HSC §1796.44(a)-(d) is stated as in effect through 12/31/2026 and was reenacted by SB 412 (Stats. 2025, ch. 414). The dementia training added by HSC §1796.44(c)(6) is operative 1/1/2027. Fees and forms are set by CDSS and change.
- Record each revision with its date and reason. Retire superseded versions in an orderly way.

### 4. Train staff on it
- Every staff member, volunteer, and affiliated aide must be trained on the policies that apply to their role. Document the training, including date, content, trainer, and attendee signature.
- Give new hires the relevant policies at onboarding. Re-train staff whenever a policy changes materially.
- This manual supplements, and does not replace, the aide training required by HSC §1796.44 (entry-level training before providing services and annual training afterward).

### 5. Make it accessible
- Keep a current copy at the place of business and available to staff. Make sure the version in use is the version the governing body adopted.
- Be prepared to produce the manual, related records, and required documents to CDSS during inspections (see HSC §1796.52 and §1796.53).

### 6. Layout
The sections that follow address the Agency's operating areas, such as licensure and posting, personnel and clearance, training, TB clearance, service delivery and scope, abuse reporting, insurance and bonding, labor-law compliance, funding-program rules, complaints and inspections, and records. Use the Regulatory Framework section of this front matter to trace each policy to its source.
front_matter.regulatory_framework:
## Regulatory Framework

The Agency operates under the rules listed below. Each is cited as it appears in the source list. Where a source was carried forward without re-checking the full text, or where counsel should confirm a point, that is noted. This list does not cover every law that may apply to the Agency. Have counsel confirm it for the Agency's circumstances.

### A. Licensing statute: Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act

- **HSC §1796.10 et seq. (Div. 2, Ch. 13, Arts. 1-12)**: Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act. This is the governing statute. It includes Art. 6 (licensure, §§1796.32-.41), Art. 7 (HCO operating requirements, §§1796.42-.43), Art. 8 (affiliated aides, §§1796.44-.45), Art. 10 (complaints/inspections, §§1796.51-.54), and Art. 11 (enforcement, §§1796.55-.59). *The sections reviewed do not contain staffing ratios, client-rights or grievance rules, a records-retention period, or an emergency-plan rule.*
- **HSC §1796.12**: Definitions. Defines affiliated home care aide (18 or older, employed by an HCO, listed on the registry), HCO, "home care services" (non-medical services for clients who cannot perform them because of age or disability), and the public registry. Aides may not assist with medication that would otherwise require administration or oversight by a licensed health care professional.
- **HSC §1796.17**: Entities that are not home care organizations. Exempts licensed home health agencies and hospices, IHSS providers, employment agencies referring independent aides, and DDS-vendored organizations. It is used to determine who is and is not an HCO.
- **HSC §1796.37**: HCO licensure requirements and two-year renewal. Covers proof of $1M/$3M liability insurance, workers' compensation, and a $10,000 employee dishonesty bond. It also covers providing CDSS, on request, a list of affiliated aides and proof of compliance with §§1796.43, .44, and .45. Other requirements are the licensee's background exam and CDSS orientation, no outstanding fees or civil penalties, disclosure of prior roles and discipline, board member understanding of duties, cooperation with CDSS, and renewal every 2 years.
- **HSC §1796.38**: Denial, suspension and revocation. Sets the grounds to deny, suspend, or revoke an HCO license. *This section was carried forward from prior fact-checked research and its text was not re-fetched. Verify the current text.*
- **HSC §1796.42(a)**: Posting of license and business hours, in a conspicuous location visible to clients and affiliated aides.
- **HSC §1796.42(b)**: Workers' compensation. Maintain and abide by a valid policy covering affiliated aides.
- **HSC §1796.42(c)**: Employee dishonesty bond, including third-party coverage, of at least $10,000.
- **HSC §1796.42(d)**: General and professional liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 aggregate.
- **HSC §1796.42(e)**: Abuse reporting and report retention. Report suspected or known elder/dependent adult abuse as required by WIC §15630 and child abuse as required by Penal Code §§11164-11174.3. Keep a copy of each suspected-abuse report, available to CDSS during normal business hours.
- **HSC §1796.43(a)**: Registry clearance before client contact; staff clearance. Aides must be cleared on the registry before direct client contact. Staff, volunteers, and employees with contact with clients, prospective clients, or confidential client information must satisfy §§1796.23, .24, .25, .26, and .28 before that contact or access. Aides must show they are free of active TB under §1796.45. The licensee may require criminal record clearance of exempt individuals who have client contact (§1796.43(b)).
- **HSC §1796.43(a)(3)**: Immediately notify CDSS when the HCO no longer employs an individual as an affiliated home care aide.
- **HSC §1796.44(a)-(d) (in effect through 12/31/2026; reenacted by SB 412, Stats. 2025, ch. 414)**: Affiliated home care aide training. Each aide must complete training before providing services: at least 5 hours of entry-level training (2 hours orientation and 3 hours safety) before presence with a client, plus at least 5 hours of annual core-competency and population-specific training. Training may be online.
- **HSC §1796.44(c)(6) (operative 1/1/2027, SB 412, Stats. 2025, ch. 414, §2)**: Dementia training added to annual training. The 5-hour entry and annual minimums are unchanged. *The bill digest also describes dementia training before providing care. Counsel should confirm whether a pre-service dementia component is required.*
- **HSC §1796.45**: Tuberculosis examination of aides. Covers timing (90 days before employment or within 7 days after, for aides hired on or after 1/1/2016), the CDC-recommended and FDA-licensed test and chest X-ray if positive, repeat exams at least every 2 years if negative, the practitioner's certificate kept on file, the exam as a condition of employment, and transfer rules.
- **HSC §1796.49**: License fees, set by CDSS. Current schedule per CDSS: HCO license $5,603 per 2 years, change of location $100, change in corporation $200, aide registration $35. Confirm current amounts with CDSS before paying.
- **HSC §1796.51**: Complaint procedures. CDSS may establish procedures for receiving, investigating, and resolving complaints against HCOs.
- **HSC §1796.52**: Inspections, complaint investigations, abuse cross-reporting. CDSS may investigate complaints and conducts random, unannounced inspections of books, records, and premises. Refusing access is cause for license revocation. CDSS has no oversight of registered aides other than maintaining the registry. CDSS cross-reports abuse reports received under §1796.42(e) to local law enforcement and APS (adult victim) or CPS (child victim).
- **HSC §1796.53**: Department entry during business hours, with or without advance notice.

### B. Mandated reporting

- **WIC §15630**: Elder and dependent adult abuse mandated reporting. Persons with full or intermittent responsibility for the care or custody of an elder or dependent adult, paid or not, are mandated reporters. Report observed, known, or reasonably suspected abuse or neglect by telephone or confidential internet tool immediately or as soon as practicably possible, followed by a written or internet report within 2 working days. For abuse outside a long-term care facility, reports go to the adult protective services agency or local law enforcement.
- **Penal Code §§11164-11174.3** (as referenced in HSC §1796.42(e)): Child abuse reporting.

### C. Employment and labor rules

- **Labor Code §246**: Paid sick leave of at least 40 hours / 5 days per year.
- **Labor Code §2802**: Employer indemnification of necessary employee expenses, including mileage for driving between clients and on client errands. The 2026 IRS rate of 72.5 cents per mile is a common benchmark.
- **29 CFR §552.109**: Third-party employers of home care workers, including HCOs, may not claim the FLSA companionship or live-in exemptions from minimum wage and overtime.

### D. Funding-program rules (apply only if the Agency participates)

- **42 U.S.C. §1396b(l)**: Electronic visit verification (EVV) for Medicaid-funded personal care services. Applies only to Medi-Cal-funded visits. Confirm the system with DHCS or the managed care plan.
- **CDSS/DHCS joint notice (Dec. 16, 2021)**: Medi-Cal Personal Care Agencies serving the HCBA Waiver are exempt from HCO licensure. An HCO not enrolled for the waiver is not covered by this exemption.
- **DHCS Community Supports Policy Guide, Vol. 1 (updated April 2025), Personal Care and Homemaker Services (PCHS)**: A plan-offered Community Support covering eligibility, IHSS as the primary program, HCBA exclusion, and provider types. Plans contract with and pay providers. The pricing figures ($29/$33/$38 per hour) are a non-binding benchmark.

### E. CDSS application and fee guidance

- **CDSS HCS 281, Application Instructions for an HCO License (Sections A and B)**: Required application content. This includes job descriptions (B2), personnel policies covering hiring, discipline, grievance, and mandated reporting, stating that employment is conditional on fingerprint clearance, a criminal-conviction statement, TB clearance, and registry listing (B3), a training plan (B4), a program description (B5), and insurance certificates (B6). It also covers the HCS 308 designee (a licensee cannot designate itself; LLCs and corporations attach a board resolution) and the HCS 402 bond.
- **CDSS Home Care Services application fees and HCO/HCA application pages**: Fees, forms, and branch contacts (see regulators below).

### F. Regulators and contacts

| Regulator | Role | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **CDSS Community Care Licensing Division, Home Care Services Branch (HCSB)** | Licenses HCOs, maintains the Home Care Aide Registry, conducts random unannounced inspections and complaint investigations | (877) 424-5778 · HCSB@dss.ca.gov · 744 P Street, M.S. 9-14-90, Sacramento, CA 95814 · https://cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/community-care/home-care-services/home-care-org-application-process |
| **CDSS Care Provider Management Branch (Guardian)** | Live Scan background checks and online Home Care Aide registration (Guardian Applicant Portal) | 1-888-422-5669 · guardian@dss.ca.gov · https://www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/community-care/home-care-services/home-care-aide-application-process |
| **Department of Health Care Services (DHCS), Managed Care / Community Supports** | Sets CalAIM Community Supports policy (Personal Care and Homemaker Services, Respite) and the non-binding pricing resource; plans contract and pay providers | CACSPricingResource@dhcs.ca.gov · https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/calaim-transforming-medi-cal/california-community-supports-pricing-resource/ (no phone listed in source) |
| **DHCS, Home and Community-Based Alternatives (HCBA) Waiver** | Waiver Personal Care Services; Medi-Cal Personal Care Agencies serving HCBA are exempt from HCO licensure | (833) 388-4551 · HCBAlternatives@dhcs.ca.gov · https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/PCA-Exemption.pdf |
| **CDSS / County IHSS programs** | In-Home Supportive Services: county-administered, consumer-directed; pays individual providers through state payroll, not agencies | https://www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/ihss/program-data (no phone or email listed in source; contact the county IHSS office) |

**Abuse-report recipients.** Under WIC §15630 and HSC §1796.42(e), reports of abuse outside a long-term care facility go to the county adult protective services agency or local law enforcement (adult victims) and to the applicable child protective services agency or local law enforcement (child victims). Contact numbers for these agencies were not provided in the source material. Insert the Agency's local APS, CPS, and law enforcement contacts here: **[LOCAL APS / CPS / LAW ENFORCEMENT CONTACTS]**.

### G. Maintaining this framework

This list reflects the sources provided and must be kept current. The manual must be customized with Agency-specific details, adopted by the Agency's governing body, reviewed and updated whenever the law or Agency operations change, and taught to all staff, with training documented.

policies.title: Organization, Licensee, Designee and Administrator Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Licensee, board members (if any), designee(s), administrator, care supervisors, schedulers and all office management staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To define who is responsible for operating [AGENCY NAME] as a licensed Home Care Organization (HCO), so that every legal duty under the Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act has a named owner and CDSS can reach a responsible person at any time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is licensed by the California Department of Social Services (CDSS), Home Care Services Branch, to arrange non-medical home care services through employed, registered home care aides. The licensee holds final authority and responsibility for operating the HCO. The licensee must pass the CDSS background exam and complete the CDSS orientation. At least one designee, who is not the licensee, is named on form HCS 308 to act in the licensee's absence. Where the licensee is an LLC or corporation, a board resolution is attached. Roles are defined by written job descriptions submitted with the application. Qualifications are set by those job descriptions, because the Act does not prescribe an administrator license or a staffing ratio. Board members, if any, sign HCS 9165 before joining and understand that CDSS enforces the Act. The licensee discloses required prior roles and any discipline, keeps no outstanding CDSS fees or civil penalties, and cooperates promptly with CDSS.

definitions.definition: The individual or entity that holds the HCO license and has the authority and responsibility to operate the organization.
A person named on form HCS 308 to act for the licensee in the licensee's absence. A licensee cannot designate him or herself.
The person [AGENCY NAME] assigns, by job description, to manage day-to-day operations. This may be the licensee or another person.
The staff person assigned by job description to supervise aides and conduct supervisory visits.
The staff person assigned by job description to assign aides to client visits and manage the schedule.
CDSS forms. HCS 308 names the designee. HCS 9165 is signed by board members acknowledging their duties.

procedures: Before the application is filed, the licensee records the legal name of the licensee entity, its form of organization and its owners and officers in the Governance File.

The licensee passes the CDSS background exam and completes the CDSS orientation before licensure. The licensee files the completion confirmations in the Governance File within 5 business days of receipt.
The licensee names at least one designee on form HCS 308. The licensee may not name him or herself. The designee's name, title and [PHONE] are entered in the Governance File.

If the licensee is an LLC or corporation, the governing body adopts a board resolution authorizing the designee and the resolution is attached to HCS 308. The signed resolution is filed in the Governance File.
The designee acts for the licensee only when the licensee is absent. The designee is available by phone during posted business hours so CDSS and clients can reach a responsible person.

When a designee changes or leaves, the licensee submits a revised HCS 308 to the Home Care Services Branch at (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov and files the confirmation. This is done before the change takes effect where possible, and otherwise within 5 business days.

The licensee approves a written job description for each position: licensee/owner, designee, administrator, care supervisor, scheduler and home care aide. The descriptions state duties, reporting line, required clearances and qualifications. Each is signed and dated by the licensee.

The administrator manages daily operations. This includes enforcing the manual, supervising office staff, reviewing incident reports and escalating serious matters to the licensee the same business day.

Each board member signs HCS 9165 before joining the board. The licensee files the signed forms in the Governance File and confirms at each board orientation that members understand CDSS enforces the Act.

The licensee completes a written disclosure of any prior role as administrator, officer, director, general partner or owner of 10% or more of a community care, residential care, child day care or home care licensee, and of any discipline. The disclosure is kept current and updated within 10 business days of any change.

The administrator keeps a ledger of CDSS fees, renewal notices and any civil penalties. Every CDSS invoice is paid by its due date, and any penalty is brought to the licensee within 1 business day of receipt so that no amount is outstanding.

Any CDSS request is logged on the day received, with date, requester, what was asked and due date. The designee or administrator responds by the stated deadline and files the response with the log entry. See GOV-07.

The licensee reviews all job descriptions, the designee assignment and the disclosures annually, and after any change in ownership or structure, and records the review date in the Governance File. See GOV-03.
The licensee holds quarterly governance meetings, or more often if needed, to review complaints, incidents and audit results and records the minutes. See GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Holds final responsibility for operating the HCO, passes the CDSS exam, completes orientation, names the designee, approves job descriptions, makes required disclosures and ensures fees and penalties are paid.
Acts for the licensee in the licensee's absence, is reachable by CDSS and clients, and responds to CDSS requests.
Manages daily operations, supervises office staff, enforces policies and escalates serious matters to the licensee.
Sign HCS 9165 before joining and understand that CDSS enforces the Act.
Perform the duties in their approved job descriptions and report compliance issues to the administrator.

documentation: Governance File with licensee identification, CDSS exam and orientation confirmations
Signed HCS 308 and board resolution (if LLC/corporation) and all revisions
Signed job descriptions with review dates
Signed HCS 9165 for each board member
Prior-role and discipline disclosures
CDSS fee and penalty ledger
CDSS request log and responses
Governance meeting minutes

policies.title: Licensure, Service Area and Advertising Requirements
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, designee, intake and marketing staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] holds a current HCO license before arranging services, renews it on time, uses its license number correctly, and describes and advertises only the non-medical services it is licensed to arrange.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not arrange home care services until it holds a current HCO license issued by CDSS. The license term is 2 years. [AGENCY NAME] renews by postmarking the nonrefundable renewal fee on or before the expiration date. Because a license is required to arrange non-medical home care through employed, registered aides, [AGENCY NAME] documents the basis for its licensure and does not rely on any exemption unless counsel confirms it applies. [AGENCY NAME] advertises and describes only non-medical services and does not offer skilled nursing, therapy, or medication assistance that would require a licensed health care professional. Its service area is defined in the program description.

definitions.definition: An organization licensed by CDSS that arranges home care services by affiliated home care aides.

Non-medical services for a client who cannot perform them because of age or disability, such as bathing, dressing, feeding, toileting, transferring, housekeeping, meals, laundry, transportation, shopping and companionship.
A person 18 or older who is employed by an HCO and listed on the Home Care Aide Registry.

Entities listed as not being HCOs in the Act, for example licensed home health agencies and hospices, IHSS individual providers, employment agencies referring independent aides, and DDS-vendored organizations. HCBA Waiver Personal Care Agencies are exempt only for that waiver service.
The document submitted with the HCO application describing services, service area, hours, population served and how aides are assigned and supervised.

procedures: No client may be accepted and no aide assigned to a client until the HCO license is issued and the license number is recorded in the Governance File.
The administrator records the license number, issue date and expiration date, and enters the expiration date on the compliance calendar with reminders at 120, 90 and 60 days.

The administrator watches for the CDSS fee notice, which CDSS mails at least 60 days before the renewal date. If no notice is received by 60 days before expiration, the administrator contacts the Home Care Services Branch at (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov and documents the contact.

Before the expiration date, the licensee confirms that the renewal fee (currently $5,603 per 2 years per the CDSS fee schedule) is paid by check or other accepted method and postmarked on or before the expiration date. A copy of the payment and mailing proof is filed.
Before renewal, the administrator confirms that no CDSS fees or civil penalties are outstanding and that the insurance, bond and aide roster are current. See GOV-06 and RR-03.

Before moving the place of business, the licensee notifies CDSS and pays the change-of-location fee (currently $100). Before any change in the corporation, the licensee notifies CDSS and pays the change-in-corporation fee (currently $200). Fees are confirmed against the CDSS fee page before payment.

The licensee reviews each new line of business, such as waiver services or Medi-Cal-funded services, with counsel before offering it. The review records whether any exemption applies. The agency does not rely on the HCBA Waiver Personal Care Agency exemption unless it is enrolled for that waiver.
The service area (counties, cities or zip codes) is written into the program description. The administrator updates it before accepting clients outside it and submits any change CDSS requires.

Before publication, all advertising, website text, brochures and social media content are reviewed by the administrator against the scope of non-medical services in SVC-01. Claims of nursing, therapy, medical or medication administration services are removed.
Advertising and written materials show the HCO license number where practical and use the legal name of the licensee. Counsel reviews advertising claims before first use and when materially changed.
Intake staff describe services only as non-medical and refer requests outside the scope to the client's physician, a home health agency or another appropriate provider. See SVC-02.
Correspondence with CDSS uses the HCO number. The administrator keeps a copy of all licensing correspondence in the Governance File.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the license is current, the renewal fee is timely paid and any change of location or corporation is reported and paid.
Maintains the compliance calendar, tracks the renewal notice, reviews advertising and keeps licensing records.
Describe only non-medical services and refer out-of-scope requests.
Reviews exemption questions and advertising claims.

documentation: Copy of HCO license with number, issue and expiration dates
Compliance calendar showing renewal reminders
Renewal fee notice, payment proof and postmark evidence
Change-of-location or change-in-corporation filings and fee receipts
Program description showing service area
Advertising review log with approval signatures
Counsel review notes on exemptions and advertising

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, designee and all staff who use or maintain the Policy & Procedure Manual of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To keep the manual, personnel policies, training plan, job descriptions and program description current, version-controlled and consistent with what CDSS has received, and to ensure legal changes such as the 2027 dementia training requirement are built in before they take effect.
policies.policy: The personnel policies, training plan, job descriptions and program description are submitted to CDSS with the HCO application. [AGENCY NAME] controls these and every policy in this manual by version number, effective date and approver. A dated copy of each document as last submitted to CDSS is retained. The manual is reviewed at least annually and whenever a statute or CDSS instruction changes. The annual cycle is an operator choice, not a state mandate. Before January 1, 2027, the annual aide training content is updated to add the special care needs of clients with dementia, as required by SB 412. The manual and training logs are kept available for CDSS inspection.

definitions.definition: A policy, job description, training plan, program description or form that carries a version number, effective date and approver.
A record of every revision showing what changed, why, who approved it and when staff were notified.
The version of an application document that CDSS most recently received.

procedures: The administrator keeps a Document Control Register listing every controlled document with title, ID, version, effective date, last review date, next review date and approver.

Each controlled document displays its ID, version number, effective date and approver on its first page. Only the current version is available in the staff manual and on the shared drive. Superseded versions are moved to an archive folder.
The administrator files a dated copy of the personnel policies, training plan, job descriptions and program description exactly as last submitted to CDSS, and labels it as the as-submitted copy.
The administrator reviews the whole manual at least once every 12 months and records the review date, reviewer and outcome in the Document Control Register.

Triggers for an immediate review include a change in statute or CDSS instruction, a CDSS inspection finding, a complaint trend, a serious incident or a new service line. The administrator opens a change request within 5 business days of learning of the trigger.
A change request states the document, the proposed change and the reason. The licensee approves or rejects it in writing. Approved changes are given a new version number and effective date.

Before 1/1/2027, the administrator and licensee add the dementia topic to the annual training content and the training plan, and update SVC-11 and PER-03 to match. The revision is recorded in the change log with the date approved.

The 5-hour entry-level and 5-hour annual training minimums are unchanged by the dementia addition. The training plan is updated to show where dementia content sits in the annual curriculum, and counsel confirms whether any pre-service dementia component is needed.

If a revision changes the personnel policies, training plan, job descriptions or program description in a way CDSS must be told about, the licensee asks the Home Care Services Branch at (877) 424-5778 how to submit the update, and files the response.
Within 10 business days of any approved revision, the administrator notifies affected staff, trains them on the change and keeps signed acknowledgments.
New hires receive the current manual during orientation and sign an acknowledgment. See PER-03.
The current manual and the training logs are kept at the place of business and produced on request during a CDSS inspection. See GOV-07.

responsibilities.duty: Approves policy changes and the as-submitted documents and ensures the annual review occurs.
Maintains the Document Control Register and change log, archives old versions, coordinates staff training on revisions.
Reports practice problems that need policy changes and ensures aides follow current versions.
Use only the current version and sign acknowledgments of updates.

documentation: Document Control Register
Change log with approvals
As-submitted copies of personnel policies, training plan, job descriptions and program description
Archive of superseded versions
Annual review records
Staff acknowledgment sheets
Record of the dementia training content update

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, designee, care supervisors and schedulers of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To give [AGENCY NAME] a routine internal audit and improvement process that finds and corrects compliance gaps before CDSS does.
policies.policy: No state quality assurance rule applies specifically to HCOs, so this program is adopted by [AGENCY NAME] by choice. CDSS verifies compliance through random, unannounced inspections that may cover books, records and premises. [AGENCY NAME] therefore audits itself on the same items: registry status, clearances before client contact, TB certificate currency, entry-level and annual training logs, insurance and bond in force, abuse-report copies, and the posted license and business hours. [AGENCY NAME] also tracks missed visits, complaints, supervisory-visit completion and aide turnover, and reports results to the licensee at least quarterly. Findings are corrected and the correction is verified.

definitions.definition: A scheduled review of records and operations against this manual and the Act.
A documented step taken to fix a finding, with an owner and a due date.
A measured item such as missed-visit rate, complaints per month, percent of supervisory visits completed, or aide turnover.

procedures: The administrator keeps an annual audit calendar with the monthly, quarterly and annual audits listed in this policy, and assigns each to a named reviewer.

Monthly, the reviewer checks each active aide's file against the registry listing and the HCS clearance record to confirm the aide was cleared on the Home Care Aide Registry before any client contact. See PER-01 and PER-02.
Monthly, the reviewer checks that every staff person, volunteer or employee with client contact or access to confidential client information was cleared before that contact or access. See PER-13.

Monthly, the reviewer checks TB documentation: that each aide's practitioner certificate is on file, that the exam was within the 90 days before hire or the 7 days after, and that the repeat date is on the calendar (every 2 years if negative). See PER-04.

Monthly, the reviewer checks the training log to confirm that each new aide completed the 5-hour entry-level training (2 hours orientation, 3 hours safety) before being present with a client, and that each aide's 5 annual hours are on track. See PER-03.

Quarterly, the reviewer confirms the general and professional liability policy, workers' compensation policy and employee dishonesty bond are in force and that certificates are filed. The reviewer also confirms the license and business hours are posted and visible. See GOV-06.
Quarterly, the reviewer confirms that every suspected-abuse report has a copy on file, with date and time of report and who made it. See SAF-01 and SAF-02.

Monthly, the care supervisor compiles the indicators: missed visits and reasons, complaints and outcomes, supervisory visits due and completed, and aide hires and separations. See SVC-04, SVC-06 and CR-02.
At least quarterly, the administrator presents audit findings and indicator trends to the licensee in a written summary.

For each finding, the licensee or administrator assigns a corrective action with an owner and a due date, normally within 30 days, and shorter for client safety matters. A client safety finding is corrected immediately.
The reviewer verifies each corrective action once it is complete and records the verification date. Findings that repeat are escalated to the licensee for a root-cause review.
The administrator uses results to decide training topics, schedule changes and policy revisions. See GOV-03.
Audit results do not include client names in documents shared outside the management team. Audit records are protected under CR-03.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews the quarterly summary, approves corrective actions and ensures resources to fix findings.
Runs the audit calendar, compiles indicators and verifies corrective actions.
Performs the assigned audit accurately and records findings.
Supplies missed-visit, complaint and supervisory-visit data and corrects practice issues with aides.

documentation: Annual audit calendar
Completed audit checklists with reviewer and date
Monthly indicator reports
Quarterly summary to the licensee
Corrective action log with owner, due date and verification date

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, designee, billing and scheduling staff, care supervisors and home care aides of [AGENCY NAME]
federal: 31 U.S.C. §3729 (False Claims Act — applies if Medi-Cal/Medicaid funds are billed)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services actually provided, protects clients and payers from fraud, and avoids conduct that could lead to denial, suspension or revocation of its license.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills only for hours actually worked by an aide, supported by timekeeping records or, for Medi-Cal-funded visits, electronic visit verification. Private-pay invoices must match the rates in the signed service agreement and the timekeeping records. Medi-Cal-funded hours are billed under the contract with the managed care plan. Plans negotiate rates with providers, and the DHCS hourly benchmark is non-binding and is not a rate. The grounds for denial, suspension or revocation of an HCO license are in the Act, and [AGENCY NAME] treats billing fraud as grounds for discipline and report. The employee dishonesty bond required of every HCO is kept in force. [AGENCY NAME] provides an internal channel for reporting billing concerns and prohibits retaliation.

definitions.definition: Billing only for services actually delivered, at the agreed rate, for the actual time worked.
Knowingly submitting or causing a false claim or invoice, including billing for visits not made, time not worked or services not provided.
The federal law that imposes liability for knowingly submitting false claims to government-funded programs such as Medicaid (Medi-Cal).
An electronic record of the date, time, location, service and aide for a visit, required for Medicaid-funded personal care services.
A bond of at least $10,000, including third-party coverage, required of every HCO.

procedures: Before an invoice is issued, billing staff match each invoice line to the aide's time record for that visit. For Medi-Cal-funded visits, billing staff match the line to the EVV record. See SVC-07.

Billing staff may not bill for a missed, cancelled or shortened visit except as the service agreement or plan contract expressly allows. A missed visit is billed only for the time actually provided. See SVC-06.
Private-pay invoices use only the rates, minimums and fees stated in the client's signed service agreement. Any rate change follows the notice rules in CR-06.

Medi-Cal-funded services are billed only under a written contract with the managed care plan, using the plan's authorization, codes and rates. The licensee confirms the EVV system with the plan or DHCS before the first Medi-Cal visit. See SVC-10.
The administrator does not use the DHCS non-binding pricing benchmark as a billing rate. The agency rate for each plan is whatever the signed contract states.

Aides record their own time truthfully at the start and end of each visit. No one may alter a time record to increase or decrease billed hours. Any necessary correction is made by the care supervisor, with a written reason, the date and the aide's signature, and the original entry is preserved.

Each month, a person other than the one who prepared the invoices reviews a sample of invoices against time records and service agreements. The reviewer documents results and sends discrepancies to the administrator.

Any overbilling found is corrected and the overpayment is refunded or credited to the client or payer within 30 days of discovery, with a written explanation. The licensee is informed of the amount and cause the same business day.

Staff who suspect fraud or a billing error report it to the administrator or the licensee. If the concern involves the administrator, the report goes to the licensee. Reports may be made orally or in writing, and may be anonymous. See CR-02.
No one may retaliate against anyone who makes a good-faith report. The licensee investigates retaliation complaints and takes disciplinary action up to termination.

The administrator opens an investigation within 2 business days of a credible report, keeps the file confidential, and the licensee decides on corrective action. Where fraud against a government payer is found, the licensee consults counsel on repayment and reporting obligations.
The licensee keeps the employee dishonesty bond (at least $10,000, with third-party coverage) in force at all times and notifies the bond carrier when required by the bond terms. See GOV-06.
All staff with billing or timekeeping duties receive this policy at hire and annually and sign an acknowledgment. See PER-03.
Billing and timekeeping records are retained under RR-01 and produced to CDSS, the payer or an auditor on a lawful request.

responsibilities.duty: Sets a culture of compliance, decides corrective action on fraud findings, keeps the bond in force.
Oversees billing accuracy, investigates reports and manages payer contracts.
Bill only verified time at agreed rates and flag discrepancies.
Approves time corrections with documentation and watches for irregular timekeeping.
Record time accurately and report concerns.

documentation: Invoices with supporting time or EVV records
Monthly invoice audit results
Time-record correction forms with reasons and signatures
Refund and credit records
Reports of billing concerns and investigation files
Employee dishonesty bond certificate
Annual compliance acknowledgments

policies.title: Required Insurance, Employee Dishonesty Bond and Postings
policies.applies_to: Licensee, administrator, designee and the staff responsible for insurance, finance and the place of business of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To ensure the required insurance and bond are never allowed to lapse and that the license, business hours and other CDSS-required information are posted where clients and aides can see them.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps the following in force at all times: general and professional liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 aggregate; a valid workers' compensation policy covering affiliated aides; and an employee dishonesty bond with third-party coverage of at least $10,000, filed on form HCS 402 with the State of California as beneficiary. Proof of workers' compensation shows the policy number, effective and expiration dates, and the carrier's name and address. The license, business hours and any other information CDSS requires are posted in a conspicuous location at the place of business, visible to clients and aides. A designated person tracks all expiration dates. A lapse is a violation of operating requirements and is treated as an urgent matter.

definitions.definition: Insurance covering claims of bodily injury, property damage and professional errors arising from services, at the required limits of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 aggregate.
Insurance required by law covering employees, including affiliated aides, for work-related injury or illness.
A bond of at least $10,000, including third-party coverage, protecting against loss from dishonest acts of employees. It is filed with CDSS on form HCS 402.
The office address on the HCO license where records are kept and the public can visit.
Document from the carrier or broker showing coverage, limits, policy number and dates.

procedures: Before the application is filed, the licensee obtains general and professional liability coverage at no less than $1,000,000 per occurrence and $3,000,000 aggregate and files the certificate in the Governance File.

Before the application is filed, the licensee obtains workers' compensation coverage for all affiliated aides. The administrator confirms the proof shows the policy number, effective and expiration dates, and the carrier's name and address.

Before the application is filed, the licensee obtains the employee dishonesty bond of at least $10,000 with third-party coverage. The bond is completed on form HCS 402 with the State of California as beneficiary and a copy is filed.

The insurance certificates are submitted with the application and with each renewal as CDSS requires. The administrator confirms the policy limits on each certificate meet the stated minimums before submission.
The administrator keeps an Insurance and Bond Register listing each policy, carrier, broker contact, policy number, limits, effective date and expiration date.
The administrator enters each expiration date on the compliance calendar with reminders at 90, 60, 30 and 14 days before expiration. The licensee is copied on all reminders.
At least 30 days before expiration, the administrator obtains the renewal or replacement and confirms the new term begins on or before the day the old one ends, with no gap in coverage.
Within 5 business days of any renewal or change, the administrator files the new certificate or bond and updates the register. The administrator sends updated proof to CDSS where it is required.

If any policy or bond is cancelled, non-renewed or about to lapse and cannot be replaced before the expiration date, the administrator informs the licensee the same day. The licensee decides immediately whether services must stop until coverage is restored, consults counsel, and contacts the Home Care Services Branch at (877) 424-5778.
The administrator reports any injury, claim or loss that may trigger coverage to the carrier promptly and within the policy's notice time. See PER-12 and SAF-03.

The administrator posts the HCO license and the business hours in a conspicuous place at the place of business, where clients and aides can see them, and posts any other information CDSS requires. See also PER-12 for workers' compensation postings.

Each month, the administrator walks the office, confirms the postings are current, legible and visible, and replaces any that are damaged or outdated. A hours-change is posted the day it takes effect.
Each quarter, the reviewer verifies the register against the certificates on file and records the result in the audit log. See GOV-04.
Certificates and the bond are produced to CDSS on request and during any inspection. See GOV-07.

responsibilities.duty: Obtains and pays for required coverage and the bond and decides on urgent action if coverage is threatened.
Keeps the register and calendar, obtains renewals, files certificates and maintains the postings.
Pay premiums on time and notify the administrator of any notice of cancellation or non-payment.
Ensures the postings are in place and certificates can be produced when the licensee is absent.

documentation: Certificates of insurance for general and professional liability
Workers' compensation proof showing policy number, dates, carrier name and address
Employee dishonesty bond (HCS 402) and carrier confirmation
Insurance and Bond Register
Compliance calendar with reminders
Monthly posting check log
Quarterly audit record

policies.title: CDSS Inspections, Complaint Investigations and Enforcement Response
policies.applies_to: Licensee, designee, administrator, all office staff, schedulers, supervisors and aides
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is always ready for a random, unannounced California Department of Social Services (CDSS) Home Care Services Branch (HCSB) inspection or complaint investigation. It also sets out how the agency cooperates fully, records what happens and corrects any finding promptly, so the Home Care Organization license is protected.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] cooperates fully and immediately with CDSS. CDSS verifies compliance through random, unannounced inspections and may investigate complaints (HSC §1796.52(a)-(b)). It may enter the HCO during posted business hours with or without advance notice (HSC §1796.53). Inspections may cover books, records and premises, and refusing access to any of them is cause for license revocation (HSC §1796.52(c)). No employee may delay, refuse, obstruct or retaliate in connection with an inspection or complaint. Grounds to deny, suspend or revoke a license are set out in HSC §1796.38, so every inspection finding is treated as a compliance matter to be corrected and tracked. CDSS has no oversight of registered aides other than maintaining the registry (HSC §1796.52(d)); the agency stays responsible for its own aides' clearance, TB, training and supervision records.

definitions.definition: The CDSS Community Care Licensing Division, Home Care Services Branch, which licenses Home Care Organizations, maintains the Home Care Aide Registry and conducts inspections and complaint investigations. Contact: (877) 424-5778, HCSB@dss.ca.gov.
A visit by CDSS staff, without advance notice, to verify compliance with the Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act.
The hours the agency has posted at its licensed office as its hours of operation. CDSS may enter during these hours.
The on-site or immediately retrievable set of records an inspector is likely to request (see Procedures).
The person named to CDSS on the HCS 308 to act for the licensee. The designee is [DESIGNEE NAME].

procedures: The licensee posts the agency's business hours at the licensed office entrance and keeps them current. A person authorized to admit inspectors and retrieve records is on site during all posted hours.

The administrator gives every office employee, scheduler and supervisor written instructions at hire and annually: greet CDSS staff courteously, ask for identification, give immediate access to the premises and records, and notify the designee at [PHONE] right away. Nobody asks an inspector to wait or return later.

The front-desk employee who greets the inspector records the arrival time and the inspector's name and title, and notifies the designee and administrator immediately. If the designee is not on site, the designee or administrator reaches the office by phone and an authorized staff member proceeds with the inspection in the meantime.

The designee or administrator escorts the inspector, answers questions truthfully and provides requested records without delay. Staff do not alter, back-date, remove or destroy any record before or during an inspection.

The administrator keeps an inspection binder on site or immediately retrievable electronically. It contains: (a) the current aide roster showing, for each aide, registry status, criminal-record clearance, TB clearance and training completion; (b) the license, current insurance certificates and the employee dishonesty bond; (c) copies of abuse reports made under SAF-01 and SAF-02; (d) personnel and client records; (e) the training plan, job descriptions, personnel policies and program description filed with the application; and (f) the complaint log and the inspection log.
The administrator verifies the binder contents monthly and signs the binder checklist. Gaps are corrected within 5 business days.
If the inspector asks for copies, the designee makes and logs them (document, date, number of pages). The agency keeps its own copy of everything provided.

Client and employee confidentiality is respected. Records are given to CDSS as the law requires, and the agency does not use confidentiality as a reason to refuse access. Questions about disclosure go to the designee and, if needed, counsel, but access is never delayed while the question is resolved.
Aides or office staff who are interviewed by an inspector may speak freely. The agency does not coach, discourage or retaliate against anyone for talking with CDSS.
At the exit discussion the designee takes notes, asks the inspector to identify each finding and the record or rule involved, and asks how and by when CDSS expects correction.

For a complaint investigation, the designee tells the administrator and licensee the same day, collects the relevant records, and prepares a timeline. Where a client complaint reached the agency first, the designee confirms CR-02 was followed.

Within 1 business day after the visit the designee completes an entry in the CDSS Inspection and Complaint Log: date, time, inspector, reason (random or complaint), records requested, findings, and the person responsible for correction.

For each finding the administrator writes a corrective action plan with the action, the responsible person and a completion date. The plan is completed on or before any deadline in CDSS's written notice. If the notice sets no date, the agency standard is 10 business days (suggested).

The agency responds in writing to any CDSS notice, citation or enforcement action by the deadline stated in the notice. The licensee and counsel review the response before it is sent. The licensee reviews any notice that could lead to denial, suspension or revocation under HSC §1796.38 immediately.
The administrator verifies completion of each corrective action, attaches proof to the log, and reports results to the licensee and to the Quality Assurance review under GOV-04.

Any suspected abuse that comes to light during an inspection or complaint is reported under SAF-01 or SAF-02 without waiting for the investigation to conclude. CDSS cross-reports abuse reports it receives to local law enforcement and Adult or Child Protective Services; the agency does not rely on CDSS to make the agency's own report.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures business hours are posted and staffed, supports full cooperation, approves written responses to CDSS and reviews enforcement notices personally.
Receives CDSS staff, directs access to records and premises, maintains the inspection and complaint log, and leads corrective action.
Maintains the inspection binder, trains office staff on inspector access, and verifies corrective actions are completed.
Give inspectors immediate courteous access and notify the designee without delay; never obstruct or alter records.
Cooperate truthfully with CDSS and notify the office if an inspector or CDSS staff contacts them.

documentation: CDSS Inspection and Complaint Log (date, inspector, scope, findings, corrective action, completion date)
Copies of records provided to CDSS, with a copy log
Exit-discussion notes and any written CDSS notice or report
Corrective action plans with proof of completion
Written responses to CDSS
Monthly inspection-binder checklist
Staff acknowledgments of inspector-access instructions

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: All clients and their representatives; all aides, supervisors and office staff
policies.purpose: To state the rights every client of [AGENCY NAME] can expect, to make sure each client receives them in writing at intake, and to make sure every aide is trained on them.
policies.policy: The Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act does not contain a client bill of rights, so [AGENCY NAME] adopts the Client Rights and Responsibilities below as agency policy. Every client or legal representative receives a written copy at intake, before services begin, and signs an acknowledgment. Annual aide training must cover clients' rights and safety (HSC §1796.44(c)), and this policy is the basis for that training. The agency complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act and provides reasonable accommodations for clients with disabilities. These rights are agency-adopted; they do not limit any right the client has under other law.

definitions.definition: A person who receives or has applied to receive non-medical home care from [AGENCY NAME].
A person legally authorized to act for the client, such as an agent under a power of attorney or a conservator.
The written statement of client rights and responsibilities adopted by this policy.
Whether an aide is listed as a Home Care Aide on the CDSS Home Care Aide Registry.

procedures: The administrator maintains the Client Rights and Responsibilities form. It lists: (a) to be treated with dignity and respect; (b) to be free from abuse, neglect, exploitation and discrimination; (c) to privacy and confidentiality; (d) to take part in developing and changing the service plan; (e) to refuse any service or ask for a different one; (f) to be told the aide's name and registry status; (g) to receive a written service agreement with rates and billing terms; (h) to have personal property respected; and (i) to complain to the agency and to CDSS HCSB at (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov without retaliation.

The form also lists client responsibilities (agency standard): to give accurate information about needs and contacts; to provide a reasonably safe home; to tell the agency about changes in health or schedule; to treat aides respectfully; and to follow the service agreement.

The intake coordinator gives the form to the client or representative at the intake visit, before the first service, and reads or explains it in the client's preferred language, or by interpreter or large print as needed (see CR-05).
The client or representative signs and dates the acknowledgment. If the client cannot or will not sign, the intake coordinator records the reason and the date delivered.
The intake coordinator leaves a copy in the client's home and uploads the signed acknowledgment to the client record within 1 business day.

The intake coordinator tells the client the name of each assigned aide and that the client may ask for the aide's registry status at any time. The office confirms that status from the registry before assignment (see PER-01 and RR-03).

Clients may refuse any service. The aide respects the refusal, tells the supervisor the same day and documents it in the visit record. The supervisor reviews the service plan if the refusal affects safety (see SVC-03 and SVC-08).
The administrator gives every aide this policy at orientation and includes clients' rights in the annual training plan (see PER-03). The training log records attendance and date.
Aides who observe or learn of a rights violation report it to the supervisor immediately. Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported under SAF-01 and not only internally.
Supervisors check at each supervisory visit that the client has the rights form and knows how to complain, and document the check (see SVC-04).
The administrator reviews the form yearly, and whenever the law changes, under GOV-03, and re-distributes it to active clients when it is materially revised.
Rights complaints are handled under CR-02 and tracked in the QA review under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains and reviews the Bill of Rights, ensures it is part of orientation and annual training, and ensures every client receives it.
Delivers and explains the Bill of Rights before services start, obtains the signed acknowledgment and records it.
Verifies at supervisory visits that rights are honored and that clients know how to complain.
Honor client rights in every visit, respect refusals and report any rights concern to the supervisor.
Receives the rights, raises concerns and follows the client responsibilities.

documentation: Signed Client Rights and Responsibilities acknowledgment in the client record
Interpreter or alternate-format use noted at intake
Aide training log showing clients' rights topic and date
Service refusal notes in visit records
Supervisory visit checklist entry on rights
Policy review record (GOV-03)

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
policies.applies_to: Clients, client representatives, family members, aides and all staff who receive or handle complaints
policies.purpose: To give clients and others a clear, safe way to raise concerns with [AGENCY NAME], to make sure each complaint is acknowledged, investigated and resolved promptly, and to tell clients about their right to go to CDSS.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] welcomes complaints and treats each as a chance to improve. The agency's personnel policies include a grievance procedure, as the HCS 281 application requires, and the client complaint process is kept consistent with it. Clients may also complain directly to CDSS HCSB at (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov. CDSS may establish procedures for receiving and resolving complaints (HSC §1796.51) and may investigate them (HSC §1796.52(a)). State law sets no complaint time frames, so the agency adopts its own standard: acknowledge within 2 business days and resolve in writing within 30 days (suggested). The agency never retaliates against a client, family member or employee for making a complaint. A complaint that alleges abuse, neglect or exploitation is also handled under SAF-01.

definitions.definition: Any oral or written expression of dissatisfaction or concern about services, staff, billing or conduct, whether or not the person calls it a complaint.
The client, representative, family member, aide or other person raising the concern.
A written response to the complainant describing what was reviewed, the outcome and any follow-up.
Any adverse action, such as reduced service, reassignment, discipline or discharge, taken because someone complained.

procedures: At intake, the intake coordinator gives each client a written complaint notice that explains how to complain to [AGENCY NAME] (phone [PHONE], mail [ADDRESS], in person or through any staff member) and how to complain to CDSS HCSB at (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov. The notice states that complaints will not lead to retaliation.

Any employee who receives a complaint, orally or in writing, records it the same day on the Complaint Intake Form: date, complainant, client, aide involved, nature of concern and any immediate safety issue. Employees must not discourage, argue with or ignore a complaint.
The employee gives the form to the administrator within 1 business day. The administrator assigns a complaint number and enters it in the Complaint Log.

The administrator screens for urgent issues. If there is an immediate risk to a client, the administrator acts at once (for example, removing the aide from the case pending review) and follows SAF-08 as needed.

If the complaint alleges abuse, neglect, abandonment, isolation or financial exploitation, the administrator makes sure the mandated report is made under SAF-01 without delay and that the incident is also documented under SAF-03.
The administrator sends the complainant a written or oral acknowledgment within 2 business days, in the client's preferred language, naming the person handling the complaint (agency standard).
The administrator, or a supervisor not involved in the care, investigates. This includes reviewing records, interviewing the complainant, the aide and others, and reviewing visit and time records.
The administrator keeps the identity of the complainant confidential to the extent possible and limits discussion to those who need to know.
The administrator decides on corrective action (for example retraining, schedule change, aide reassignment, billing correction or discipline under PER-07) and documents the decision.

The administrator sends a written resolution letter within 30 days of receipt (agency standard). If more time is needed, the administrator sends a written status update before day 30 and states the new expected date.

Each resolution letter reminds the complainant of the right to contact CDSS HCSB at (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov if not satisfied. The agency's resolution process does not replace or delay the complainant's right to go to CDSS.
Employee grievances follow the grievance procedure in the personnel policies. The administrator ensures the two procedures are consistent when either is revised under GOV-03.
The administrator reviews the Complaint Log quarterly, identifies trends and presents results to the QA review under GOV-04.
If CDSS contacts the agency about a complaint, the designee follows GOV-07 and cooperates fully.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the complaint process, logs, investigates or assigns, issues resolution letters and reports trends.
Gives the complaint notice at intake and explains how to reach the agency and CDSS.
Accept every complaint, record it the same day, forward it within 1 business day and never retaliate.
Assists with investigations and follow-up and checks at supervisory visits that clients know how to complain.
Reviews complaint trends and any complaint that involves the administrator or a serious allegation.

documentation: Complaint Intake Form
Complaint Log with complaint number, dates acknowledged and resolved, and outcome
Investigation notes and interview records
Acknowledgment and resolution letters
Corrective action records
Quarterly complaint trend report

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
policies.applies_to: All employees, aides, volunteers, schedulers, supervisors, contractors and anyone with access to client information
policies.purpose: To protect the privacy and confidentiality of client information in every form, and to set clear rules for who may see it, how it is stored and how privacy problems are handled.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps all client information confidential. Any staff person, volunteer or employee who has contact with clients or access to confidential client information must first satisfy the clearance requirements of HSC §1796.43(a)(1); no one gets access until that is complete. HIPAA applies directly if the agency is a covered entity, for example if it conducts standard electronic transactions with health plans. If it is not, the agency adopts the HIPAA standards by policy. The licensee decides and documents covered-entity status with counsel. California medical-privacy and breach-notification laws apply in addition; counsel adds those section citations to this policy. Client information is shared only as needed for care, billing, supervision or as legally required. Reports of suspected abuse are both permitted and required (see SAF-01).

definitions.definition: Any information that identifies a client or relates to the client's health, care, finances, address, schedule or home, in any form.
A health plan, health care clearinghouse or health care provider that conducts standard electronic transactions, as defined in 45 CFR 160.103.
Individually identifiable health information held or transmitted by a covered entity.
An unauthorized acquisition, access, use or disclosure of client information that compromises its privacy or security.
The person responsible for developing and implementing privacy policies, designated by the licensee: [PRIVACY OFFICER NAME].

procedures: Within 30 days of licensure, the licensee and counsel determine whether the agency is a HIPAA covered entity and record the decision, the reasons and the date in the Privacy Determination Memo. The memo is reviewed whenever billing arrangements change, such as new health-plan contracts (see SVC-10).

The licensee designates a Privacy Officer, [PRIVACY OFFICER NAME], responsible for this policy, staff training, privacy complaints and breach response. This follows 45 CFR 164.530 for covered entities and is agency policy if not covered.

The office confirms that each person has satisfied the clearance requirements under HSC §1796.43(a)(1) before granting access to client records or contact with clients, prospective clients or their information (see PER-02 and PER-13). The administrator keeps proof in the personnel file.
All staff sign a Confidentiality Agreement at hire and annually. It states that they may use client information only to do their jobs.

Staff receive privacy training at orientation and annually, covering what is confidential, permitted uses, safe storage, mobile devices and how to report a privacy concern. The training log records dates (see PER-03).

Staff may share client information only: (a) with those involved in the client's care or supervision; (b) for billing and payment; (c) as the client or representative authorizes in writing; and (d) as required by law, including abuse reports to APS, law enforcement or CDSS (see SAF-01).
Staff do not discuss clients in public, with friends or family, or on social media. Photos, videos or posts about clients or their homes are prohibited without written client authorization.
Paper records are kept in locked cabinets in the office and are not left in vehicles. Aides keep only what is needed for the visit in the home and return paper records to the office.

Electronic records are kept in password-protected systems with unique user logins, with access limited to what each role needs. Staff do not share passwords. The administrator removes access on the day an employee separates (see PER-11).

Texts and e-mails containing client information use only agency-approved, secure channels, and the minimum information needed. Staff do not store client information on personal devices unless the device is protected as the administrator requires.

If the agency is a covered entity, the Privacy Officer prepares a Notice of Privacy Practices consistent with 45 CFR 164.520, gives it to each client at intake, makes a good-faith effort to obtain a signed acknowledgment, and posts it in the office.
Clients may ask to see or get a copy of their records and to request corrections. The Privacy Officer responds in writing within 30 days (agency standard) and documents the response.
Any employee who knows or suspects that information was lost, stolen, misdirected or improperly accessed reports it to the Privacy Officer immediately, and no later than the same business day.

The Privacy Officer investigates within 2 business days, contains the problem and documents the facts. If the agency is a covered entity, the officer follows the HIPAA breach rule (45 CFR 164.400-414), including notifying affected individuals without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery. Counsel advises on any California breach-notice duties.
Violations lead to discipline under PER-07, up to termination. The agency does not retaliate against anyone who reports a privacy concern.
The Privacy Officer reviews this policy yearly under GOV-03 and reports privacy incidents to the QA review under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Decides covered-entity status with counsel, designates the Privacy Officer and provides resources for safeguards.
Maintains privacy practices, trains staff, handles access requests and complaints, and leads breach response.
Verifies clearance before access is granted, manages user access and ensures records are secured.
Protect confidential information, share it only as permitted, and report suspected privacy incidents immediately.

documentation: Privacy Determination Memo (covered-entity decision)
Signed Confidentiality Agreements
Privacy training logs
Proof of clearance before access (personnel files)
Notice of Privacy Practices and acknowledgments, if covered
Access, amendment and authorization request records
Privacy incident and breach investigation files
System access and termination logs

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
policies.applies_to: All aides, supervisors, office staff, schedulers and volunteers
policies.purpose: To protect clients from theft, financial abuse and undue influence, to set strict rules for handling client money and property, and to make sure suspected exploitation is reported as the law requires.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] has zero tolerance for theft or financial exploitation of clients. Financial abuse is one of the forms of abuse that must be reported under WIC §15630, so suspected financial exploitation by anyone, including our own staff, is a mandated report (see SAF-01). The agency carries the employee dishonesty bond of at least $10,000, including third-party coverage, that HSC §1796.42(c) requires. That bond is the statutory backstop for employee theft; it does not replace the controls in this policy. Aides may shop for groceries and personal-care items for clients as part of the scope of services (see SVC-01). All shopping and handling of money is subject to the agency-adopted controls below.

definitions.definition: Taking, using, hiding or appropriating a client's money or property for any wrongful use or with intent to defraud, or by undue influence.
Cash given by the client or representative for a specific purchase, logged on the Errand Funds Form.
Anything of value given to an employee by a client or family member, including money, items, loans or property.
A bond of at least $10,000 with third-party coverage, maintained under HSC §1796.42(c).

procedures: At orientation and each year, the administrator trains staff on this policy and the signed Property and Gift Rules. Aides sign an acknowledgment that violations can lead to termination and reporting to law enforcement (see PER-03 and PER-07).

Aides must not use, hold or ask for a client's credit or debit cards, checks, bank PINs, passwords or account access. Aides must not borrow from or lend money to a client, or sell or buy anything from or for the client for personal benefit.

Aides must not accept gifts of money or items of value. If a client offers a gift, the aide politely declines and tells the supervisor at the next contact. A small token, such as a card or homemade treat, may be accepted if the supervisor is told the same day and records it (agency standard).

Aides and office staff must not be named in a client's will, trust, power of attorney or beneficiary designation, add themselves as a signer on any account, or help the client prepare such documents. An aide who learns of such a request tells the supervisor immediately.

Cash handling is limited to errand funds. For each errand, the aide completes the Errand Funds Form: amount received, purchase, receipt, change returned and the client's or representative's signature. Receipts are required for every purchase, and the aide returns the change and receipt to the client at the visit.

Aides must not keep client cash overnight or mix client money with their own. Aides do not pay client bills or make bank transactions unless the service plan says so and the administrator has approved a written procedure.

At intake the supervisor and client list valuables in the home that need extra care, such as jewelry, cash or firearms, and record any concerns. Aides do not move, hold or remove client valuables for storage.
Aides report any damage to, or loss of, client property to the supervisor the same day. The supervisor records it as an incident under SAF-03 and tells the client or representative.
The office reviews Errand Funds Forms and receipts monthly against client billing and notes. The administrator investigates differences within 5 business days.

If an aide, employee or any other person is suspected of financial exploitation, theft or undue influence, the person who becomes aware tells the administrator or designee immediately. A mandated reporter does not need approval to report.

The mandated reporter must report by phone or confidential internet tool to the county adult protective services agency or local law enforcement immediately or as soon as practicably possible. A written or internet report follows within 2 working days (WIC §15630). The reporter's copy goes to the incident file (see SAF-01).

The administrator tells the client or representative of suspected theft the same day, and tells the designee. The agency removes the suspected employee from the client's case immediately pending review, and does not discuss the allegation with the employee in a way that interferes with law enforcement.
The licensee, with counsel and the insurer or bond issuer, decides whether to file a claim under the employee dishonesty bond. The administrator keeps the bond information current under GOV-06.
The administrator reports cases to the QA review under GOV-04 and revises controls as needed.

responsibilities.duty: Follow all property, gift and money rules, keep receipts, and report any suspected exploitation immediately.
Reviews errand forms, trains aides in the home, takes gift reports and acts on concerns the same day.
Audits Errand Funds Forms monthly, investigates losses, coordinates reports and bond claims.
Is told the same day of any suspected theft and ensures reports and client notification are completed.
Maintains the employee dishonesty bond and supports prompt reporting and removal of suspected employees.

documentation: Signed Property and Gift Rules acknowledgments
Errand Funds Forms with receipts
Monthly audit notes
Gift and attempted-gift reports
Incident reports for loss, damage or theft (SAF-03)
Copies of abuse reports and written follow-up filed with APS or law enforcement
Client or representative notification record
Employee dishonesty bond and any claim file

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
policies.applies_to: All employees, aides, supervisors, schedulers and intake staff
federal: Title VI, 42 U.S.C. §2000d (if the HCO receives federal financial assistance)
policies.purpose: To make sure every person who seeks or receives services from [AGENCY NAME] is treated fairly and respectfully, can understand the services and their rights, and receives reasonable accommodation for disability.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] serves clients without discrimination by race, color, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, age or source of payment. Services are subject only to the agency's licensed service area and scope of services and its ability to meet the client's needs safely. The Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act sections reviewed contain no HCO-specific nondiscrimination or language-access rule, so this is an agency-adopted policy that also carries out the federal Americans with Disabilities Act and, if the agency receives federal financial assistance, Title VI. California civil rights statutes also apply; counsel adds the section citations to this policy. The agency provides interpreter or translated-document access and reasonable accommodations for clients with disabilities. Aides are trained on respectful, culturally competent care as part of annual 'clients' rights' training (HSC §1796.44(c)).

definitions.definition: Treating a person less favorably, or denying or limiting services, because of a protected characteristic listed in this policy.
A limited ability to speak, read, write or understand English well enough to take part in care and services.
A change in policy, practice or communication that lets a person with a disability use services equally, unless it would fundamentally alter the service or cause undue burden.
