Registry verification, Live Scan clearance and signed conviction statement
TB certificates
Entry-level and annual training logs
Form I-9 and payroll records
Quarterly file audit records
CDSS request log and copies of records provided
Retention schedule and destruction log

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
policies.applies_to: All affiliated home care aides, payroll staff, schedulers, supervisors and the Administrator
policies.purpose: To make sure every aide is paid at least the applicable minimum wage and overtime for all hours worked, and that [AGENCY NAME] does not rely on exemptions that are unavailable to a licensed Home Care Organization.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is a third-party employer of home care workers. Under 29 CFR §552.109, it may not claim the federal companionship or live-in exemptions from minimum wage and overtime. The Agency pays minimum wage and overtime for all hours worked and pays the higher of the California state minimum wage or the local minimum wage where the work is performed. The 2026 California minimum wage is $16.90 per hour. Local minimums are higher in many cities. Examples are City of Los Angeles $18.42; unincorporated Los Angeles County $18.47 (from 7/1/2026); San Francisco $19.61; San Diego $17.75; San Jose $18.45; West Hollywood $20.25; and Emeryville $20.34. These rates change, so payroll verifies them before each pay period and at each rate-change date. The Agency does not offer live-in, 24-hour or other extended-shift care until legal counsel has confirmed in writing how California daily overtime, meal-period, rest-break and shift rules apply to it. The Agency will also confirm with counsel whether the SB 525 health-care minimum wage applies to it. HCOs are not listed in the research reviewed, but the question is not settled for this manual. Paid sick leave is addressed in PER-09. Travel time and mileage are addressed in PER-10.

definitions.definition: All time an aide is under the Agency's control or required to be on duty, including client visit time, paid training, orientation, required meetings, documentation time and compensable travel between clients.

An employer, such as a licensed HCO, that employs a home care worker who provides services to a client who is not the employer. Third-party employers may not claim the companionship or live-in exemptions (29 CFR §552.109).
The highest of the federal, California and local (city or county) minimum wage in effect for the location where the work is performed.

Any assignment in which an aide stays overnight or works a continuous shift of 24 hours or more. These assignments are not offered unless counsel has approved the pay and scheduling method in writing.

procedures: The Administrator confirms with counsel at least annually, and each time a new service area is added, that the Agency's pay practices comply with California and federal wage and hour law. The Administrator records the date and outcome in the compliance calendar.

Payroll prepares a minimum wage schedule listing the state rate ($16.90 for 2026) and each local rate that applies to a city or county where aides work. Payroll updates the schedule on January 1, July 1 and whenever a local ordinance changes a rate.

Before each pay period closes, payroll compares every aide's regular hourly rate with the applicable minimum wage for the aide's work location. If an aide works in more than one jurisdiction, the higher rate applies to the hours worked in that jurisdiction.
The Administrator sets aide pay rates at or above the applicable minimum wage. No offer letter may state a rate below the applicable minimum.
New aides are classified as non-exempt W-2 employees at hire (PER-08). Payroll does not apply the companionship or live-in exemptions to any aide, client or funding source.

Aides record start and stop times for every visit through the timekeeping or EVV system described in SVC-07. Aides record other work time (training, meetings, travel) on the same system or the Agency's time record.
Schedulers do not assign an aide hours that would create unplanned overtime without prior approval from the Administrator or designee. Scheduling for overtime is documented on the schedule.
Payroll computes overtime for all hours worked over the limits confirmed by counsel under California and federal law. Payroll reviews the computation for each aide before payroll is released.

Aides may not work off the clock. Supervisors may not ask, permit or encourage unrecorded work, including charting, phone calls to clients or the office, or waiting time that is required by the Agency.

If an aide forgets to record time or a visit runs over, the aide notifies the scheduler the same day. The supervisor reviews and approves any time correction and documents the reason. Payroll pays all time actually worked, whether or not it was pre-approved. Unapproved overtime may be addressed through discipline, but it is never left unpaid.

The Agency does not offer live-in, 24-hour or overnight sleep-time assignments until counsel has approved in writing the pay method, meal and rest break treatment and recordkeeping for each type of assignment. The Administrator keeps the written approval in the compliance file.

Meal periods and rest breaks are scheduled and documented according to the written guidance from counsel. Schedulers build visits and shift lengths so that required breaks can be taken, and the aide records any missed break on the time record so that payroll can address it per counsel's guidance.
Payroll issues each aide an itemized wage statement each pay period showing hours worked, rates, overtime and deductions, and keeps payroll records per RR-01 and PER-05.

Once each quarter, the Administrator or designee audits a sample of timesheets against client visit records, EVV data and the schedule. The audit is reported through GOV-04, and discrepancies are corrected and any underpayment is paid on the next regular payroll.

An aide who believes he or she has been underpaid reports it to payroll or the Administrator. The Agency investigates within 10 business days, pays any amount owed on the next regular payroll, and does not retaliate against the aide for raising the concern.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures lawful pay practices; obtains and keeps counsel's confirmations; approves any live-in or extended-shift assignment; reviews quarterly audit results.
Maintains the minimum wage schedule; computes regular and overtime pay; issues wage statements; corrects errors promptly.
Builds schedules that avoid unplanned overtime and allow for breaks; flags overtime risk to the Administrator.
Reviews and approves time corrections; never permits off-the-clock work.
Records all time worked accurately and on time; reports missed breaks, missed pay or time-clock problems.

documentation: Minimum wage schedule with effective dates and sources
Written confirmations from counsel (companionship/live-in exemptions, SB 525 applicability, overtime, meal and rest break and live-in shift rules)
Timesheets, EVV and timekeeping records
Time correction approvals
Payroll registers and itemized wage statements
Quarterly timesheet audit reports and corrections
Wage complaint and resolution records

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All aides, supervisors, office staff, schedulers, administrators and volunteers
policies.purpose: To set clear conduct rules and professional boundaries that protect clients from exploitation and abuse, and to describe how violations are addressed, as required for the Agency's personnel policies (HCS 281, Section B3).
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] expects every staff member to act honestly, respectfully and professionally. Staff do not accept gifts, loans or any financial benefit from clients or their families. They do not use client property for personal reasons. They do not solicit clients to hire the aide privately. They do not post about clients on social media. They do not use drugs or alcohol while on duty. They do not bring visitors into a client's home. The Agency's personnel policies cover hiring, discipline, grievance and mandated reporting, as the licensing application requires. Failure to meet the duty to report abuse, and any exploitation of a client, are grounds for immediate suspension and termination. Aides and others with responsibility for the care of an elder or dependent adult are mandated reporters under WIC §15630 (see SAF-01).

definitions.definition: The limit that separates a paid, professional caregiving relationship from a personal, financial or social one.
Money, gifts, loans, tips, inheritance or bequest promises, property, use of a client's accounts or cards, or any other item or advantage of value received from a client or the client's family.
An arrangement in which an aide works directly for a client or the client's family, outside the Agency, in place of or in addition to Agency services.

A person with full or intermittent responsibility for the care or custody of an elder or dependent adult, paid or unpaid, who must report observed, known or reasonably suspected abuse or neglect (WIC §15630).

procedures: At hire, each staff member receives and signs the Code of Conduct and Boundaries in this policy. The signed copy is placed in the personnel file (PER-05). The Agency repeats the review at annual training (PER-03).

Staff decline gifts, tips, loans and financial benefits of any kind. If a client insists, the staff member says the Agency does not allow it and reports the offer to the supervisor the same day. The supervisor records the event, returns any item with the client's understanding, and refers the matter under CR-04 where needed.

Staff do not use a client's vehicle, home, phone, computer, food, credit or debit cards, accounts or other property for personal reasons. Use of client money or property for errands is only as authorized in the service plan and documented under CR-04.

Staff do not solicit or accept private employment from Agency clients or their families, and do not refer clients to other caregivers or agencies. A client who asks to hire the aide privately is told to speak with the Administrator.

Staff do not post any information, photos, videos or comments about clients, client homes or client care on social media or in public forums. Staff do not photograph clients except as the Agency authorizes in writing. Staff protect client information under CR-03.

Staff report to work free from the effects of alcohol, cannabis or unlawfully used drugs. They do not use or possess these on duty or in a client's home. If staff take a legally prescribed medication that may affect their work, they tell the supervisor so the work assignment can be adjusted, without disclosure of medical details.
No visitors, including family, friends, children or pets, are allowed in a client's home during a shift unless the client and the Administrator have approved it in advance.

Staff keep relationships with clients professional. This includes no romantic or sexual relationships, no borrowing or lending of money, no sharing of personal social-media accounts and no sharing of personal problems that burden the client.

Staff immediately tell their supervisor about any conflict of interest or dual relationship with a client, for example being related to a client or being named in a client's will or power of attorney. The Administrator decides whether to reassign the aide.

Staff make required reports of suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation as described in SAF-01. Staff do not delay a report to check with a supervisor. A report to APS or law enforcement is made immediately or as soon as practicably possible, followed by the written report within 2 working days, and the supervisor is informed after that.

When a boundary violation is reported or suspected, the supervisor notifies the Administrator the same business day. The Administrator may suspend the staff member from client contact pending review and begins an investigation within 1 business day.

The Administrator interviews the people involved, reviews the records and documents findings, usually within 10 business days. The Administrator imposes discipline in proportion to the facts, up to termination.

Failure to report suspected abuse when required, and any exploitation of a client, result in immediate suspension and termination. The Administrator makes the required reports to APS or law enforcement (SAF-01), files incident reports (SAF-03) and makes reports to CDSS as required in RR-02.
Staff who report a conduct concern in good faith are protected from retaliation. Retaliation is itself a violation of this policy.

Discipline is progressive for other conduct violations: verbal warning, written warning, suspension and termination, depending on the severity of the violation. Each step is documented, signed by the employee when possible and placed in the personnel file.
Employees may file a grievance about discipline or workplace treatment with the Administrator in writing within 10 business days. The Administrator responds in writing within 10 business days.

responsibilities.duty: Enforces the code of conduct; investigates alleged violations; imposes discipline; makes required reports; protects reporters from retaliation.
Reviews expectations with aides; receives reports of gifts and boundary issues; escalates concerns to the Administrator the same day.
Follow this policy; decline gifts and benefits; report abuse and neglect as mandated reporters; report conflicts of interest.
Obtains signed acknowledgments at hire and annually; maintains discipline records in the personnel file.

documentation: Signed Code of Conduct and Boundaries acknowledgment
Gift or benefit offer reports
Conflict-of-interest disclosures
Investigation notes and findings
Disciplinary notices and employee responses
Mandated reporter acknowledgments and report copies (kept per SAF-01)
Grievance records and responses

policies.title: Employment Status of Aides — W-2 Employees Only
policies.applies_to: Administrator, hiring and payroll staff, and all affiliated home care aides
policies.purpose: To make sure every aide who provides services through [AGENCY NAME] is a W-2 employee, as the Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act requires of an HCO, and that payroll obligations are met.
policies.policy: Under HSC §1796.12, an affiliated home care aide is 18 or older, is employed by an HCO and is listed on the registry. An HCO arranges home care services through affiliated aides. [AGENCY NAME] therefore employs all of its aides on a W-2 basis. Aides who contract directly with a client are independent aides and fall outside the HCO model. The Agency does not classify aides as independent contractors, does not use 1099 arrangements for aides and does not use the companionship or live-in exemptions (29 CFR §552.109). The Agency withholds taxes, pays employer payroll taxes and covers aides under workers' compensation (PER-12).

definitions.definition: A person 18 years or older who is employed by an HCO and is listed on the Home Care Aide Registry (HSC §1796.12).
A home care aide who contracts directly with a client rather than through an HCO. This is not the Agency's model.
A person whose wages are reported on IRS Form W-2, from which the employer withholds income tax and employee payroll taxes.
Taxes and contributions the Agency pays in addition to wages, including Social Security and Medicare (FICA), state unemployment insurance (UI) and the Employment Training Tax (ETT).

procedures: The Administrator confirms before opening for business that all aide positions are budgeted and offered as W-2, non-exempt employment, and that job descriptions and offer letters say so.
The Agency never offers or accepts a 1099, independent-contractor, gig-worker, referral-only or staffing-by-the-client arrangement for aides.

Before the first day of work, each new aide completes the federal and state tax withholding and employment eligibility forms, and payroll sets up the aide in payroll. The aide's first paid hour is on or after the date of hire, and orientation and training hours are paid (PER-03, PER-06).
No individual provides services under the Agency's name, assignment or supervision before being hired, cleared on the registry and entered into payroll (PER-01, PER-02).

Payroll withholds federal and California income tax and the employee's share of FICA and the employee's State Disability Insurance (SDI), currently 1.3%, from each paycheck. Payroll deposits and reports withholdings on time.

Payroll budgets and pays employer payroll costs: FICA at 7.65%; UI at 3.4% for a new employer; and ETT at 0.1%, with UI and ETT applying on the first $7,000 of wages per employee. These rates are planning figures that the Administrator verifies each year with the Employment Development Department and the Agency's payroll provider.

Aides use Agency-provided or Agency-approved supplies and follow the Agency's service plans, schedules and supervision (SVC-03, SVC-04). The Agency does not allow aides to set their own rates, to bill clients directly or to accept payment from clients.
Aides who are asked to also work privately for an Agency client are directed to follow PER-07. Private arrangements are not part of the Agency's operations.

Before any proposal to use staffing agencies, registries or contractors for caregivers, the Administrator obtains written approval from counsel and confirms HCO licensure and registry requirements. The Agency does not place unaffiliated workers in client homes.

Each year the Administrator reviews the roster of everyone providing client care and compares it with payroll and with the registry roster (RR-03), to confirm that each person is a current W-2 employee and listed as the Agency's affiliated aide.

If a worker is found to be misclassified or to have worked without being on payroll, the Administrator removes the person from client contact the same day, corrects payroll and tax filings with counsel's advice, pays any wages owed, and records the correction in the compliance file.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures W-2 status for all aides; approves any change to the staffing model with counsel; conducts the annual roster reconciliation.
Sets up new aides, withholds and remits taxes, tracks employer payroll rates, and keeps payroll records.
Makes W-2 offers, collects tax and eligibility forms and confirms no worker starts before being on payroll.
Completes employment paperwork, records time and follows Agency direction and supervision.

documentation: Offer letters and job descriptions stating W-2 non-exempt status
Tax withholding and employment eligibility forms
Payroll registers, tax deposit records and quarterly filings
Annual roster reconciliation (payroll, registry, schedule)
Counsel confirmations of employment-model questions

policies.title: Paid Sick Leave and Leaves of Absence
policies.applies_to: All employees, including aides, supervisors and office staff; schedulers and payroll staff who administer leave
policies.purpose: To give employees the paid sick leave California requires, to protect clients from exposure to contagious illness, and to explain how leave is requested, approved and protected from retaliation.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides paid sick leave of at least 40 hours or 5 days per year, as required by Labor Code §246. The Agency's plan addresses accrual or front-loading, carryover, use and the prohibition on retaliation. Employees may use sick leave for their own health needs and as the law otherwise allows. The Agency does not require an aide with symptoms of a contagious illness to work (SAF-04) and does not discipline or retaliate against an employee for lawful use of sick leave. The Agency has not verified other California or federal leave laws for this manual. Before denying any leave request, and whenever an employee asks for family, medical, pregnancy, military, jury, voting, crime-victim or other protected leave, the Administrator consults counsel to confirm what the law requires.

definitions.definition: Paid time off that employees may use for their own or a family member's health care needs and for other purposes recognized by law.
Giving the employee the full annual paid sick leave amount (not less than 40 hours or 5 days) at the start of each year, rather than accruing it hour by hour.
Fever, vomiting, diarrhea, new cough or rash, or other signs of illness that could spread to a client, as described in SAF-04.
Discipline, dismissal, reduced hours, schedule penalties or any adverse action because an employee requested or used protected leave.

procedures: The Administrator adopts a written sick leave plan that gives each employee at least 40 hours or 5 days of paid sick leave per year (Labor Code §246). The plan states the year used (calendar, anniversary or other) and whether leave is front-loaded or accrued. Counsel reviews the plan before it is adopted.

The Agency prefers to front-load 40 hours of paid sick leave on the first day of employment and at the start of each following benefit year. If the Agency instead uses accrual, counsel confirms the accrual rate, waiting periods, usage caps and carryover rules in writing before the plan is used.
Payroll shows the employee's available paid sick leave balance on each itemized wage statement or on a separate statement provided with each payment of wages.
At hire, the employee receives the written leave plan and the required notices, and signs an acknowledgment that is filed in the personnel file (PER-05).

An employee requests sick leave by telling the scheduler or supervisor as early as practicable, by phone, text or in person, ideally at least 2 hours before the shift. For foreseeable needs such as an appointment, the employee gives reasonable advance notice.

The scheduler records the request, finds a replacement aide for the client under SVC-06, and informs the client or family as needed. The Agency does not require the employee to find his or her own replacement.
The Agency does not require documentation, such as a doctor's note, as a condition for lawful use of paid sick leave, unless counsel confirms in writing that it is allowed in the specific situation.

An aide who has symptoms of a contagious illness, reports the symptoms before the shift and is told not to work. The supervisor follows SAF-04 and the aide may return when symptom-free as described there. Paid sick leave is offered for the missed shift.

If the aide has already arrived at a client's home with symptoms, the aide notifies the supervisor, leaves the home as safely as possible and the supervisor arranges coverage so the client is not left unattended (SVC-06).
Payroll pays used sick leave on the next regular payday and keeps usage and balance records.

The Agency does not count lawful sick leave use as an absence for attendance discipline and does not retaliate against any employee for using or requesting it. An employee who believes he or she was retaliated against may file a grievance under PER-07 or contact the Administrator directly.

When an employee asks for any other leave (medical, family, pregnancy, military, jury duty, bereavement, domestic violence or others), the supervisor refers the request to the Administrator within 1 business day. The Administrator confirms the legal requirements with counsel, responds to the employee in writing and documents the decision.

The Administrator reviews leave records once a year to check that all employees were given at least 40 hours or 5 days of paid sick leave, that balances were shown on wage statements and that no adverse action followed leave use. Findings are reported through GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts and reviews the paid sick leave plan with counsel; decides other leave requests after counsel review; prevents retaliation.
Tracks balances, pays used leave on the next regular payday, shows balances on wage statements.
Records sick calls, arranges coverage and informs clients without penalizing the employee.
Directs ill aides not to work; refers other leave requests to the Administrator within 1 business day.
Gives notice as early as practicable, and reports symptoms of contagious illness before a shift.

documentation: Written paid sick leave plan and counsel review
Signed employee acknowledgments
Sick leave balance and usage records
Itemized wage statements showing balances
Sick-call and coverage logs
Leave requests, counsel confirmations and Administrator decisions
Annual leave compliance review

policies.title: Travel Time, Mileage and Expense Reimbursement
policies.applies_to: All aides and supervisors who travel between clients or run client errands; payroll and scheduling staff
policies.purpose: To make sure employees are paid for compensable travel time and are reimbursed for necessary business expenses, including mileage, as California and federal law require.
policies.policy: Because [AGENCY NAME] is a third-party employer that cannot claim the companionship or live-in exemptions (29 CFR §552.109), travel between clients during the workday is compensable time. Consistent with the U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division's direct care travel-time guidance, the Agency counts this time as hours worked. Under Labor Code §2802, the Agency reimburses necessary employee expenditures, including mileage for driving between clients and on client errands. The Agency reimburses mileage at no less than the IRS standard mileage rate, which is 72.5 cents per mile for 2026. Employees record mileage by client and date on a mileage log. The Agency pays approved mileage and expense reimbursements within the next regular payroll.

definitions.definition: Time spent traveling between client homes or other work locations during the workday, which is paid as hours worked.
Driving the aide does for the client as authorized in the service plan, such as shopping, pharmacy pick-up or a trip to the post office.
A record showing the date, starting point, destination, client served, miles driven and purpose of each business trip.
The business mileage rate published by the Internal Revenue Service, which is 72.5 cents per mile for 2026 and which the Agency uses as its minimum reimbursement benchmark.

procedures: The Administrator sets the mileage reimbursement rate at no less than the IRS standard business rate, which is 72.5 cents per mile for 2026. Payroll updates the rate each January 1 and whenever the IRS changes it during the year.

At hire, each aide receives this policy and signs an acknowledgment that is filed in the personnel file (PER-05). The aide is told that travel between clients is paid time and that mileage must be logged.
The scheduler builds schedules that allow reasonable travel time between visits and shows travel segments on the schedule. The scheduler does not ask aides to travel on unpaid time between clients.

Aides record the start and end of travel between clients in the timekeeping system (SVC-07), or on the time record if the system does not capture travel. Payroll pays this time as hours worked and includes it in overtime calculations (PER-06).

Counsel provides written guidance on how the Agency treats the first trip of the day from home and the last trip of the day to home. The Administrator applies the guidance in the same way to all employees and keeps it in the compliance file.

The aide records every business trip on the mileage log the same day, with the date, from and to locations, client, miles and purpose. The aide logs odometer readings or trip distances from a mapping tool.

For client errands, the aide uses the vehicle and route authorized in the service plan, keeps receipts where money is spent and follows CR-04 for handling client money. Driving clients in the aide's vehicle follows SAF-07.
Aides submit mileage logs and expense receipts at least once each pay period. The supervisor reviews them for completeness and reasonableness within 2 business days and sends them to payroll.
Payroll pays approved mileage and expense reimbursements within the next regular payroll and shows them separately from wages on the wage statement.

Besides mileage, the Agency reimburses other necessary business expenses the aide incurs at the Agency's direction, such as supplies purchased at the Agency's request, parking, tolls and a share of work-related phone use if counsel advises it is required. The aide submits receipts, and approval is made in advance by the supervisor wherever possible.

The Agency does not require aides to carry personal vehicle insurance beyond what California requires for driving, and does not require aides to pay for any required equipment, uniforms, background checks, TB tests or training needed for the job. The Administrator checks with counsel before charging an employee any cost related to work.

If the aide believes a reimbursement was calculated incorrectly or not paid, the aide tells payroll or the Administrator. The Agency reviews the claim within 10 business days and pays any amount owed with the next regular payroll.

Each quarter payroll compares a sample of mileage logs with client schedules and EVV or time records to check for missing travel time and unclaimed mileage. Findings and corrections go to the Administrator and are reported through GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Sets the mileage rate and reimbursement rules; obtains counsel's guidance on commute questions; resolves disputes.
Pays travel time as hours worked; reimburses mileage and expenses within the next regular payroll; keeps records.
Allows paid travel time between visits; does not schedule unpaid travel between clients.
Reviews and approves mileage logs and expense claims within 2 business days.
Records travel time and mileage by client and date; submits logs and receipts each pay period.

documentation: Mileage logs by client and date
Expense reports and receipts
Travel time entries in timekeeping/EVV records
Mileage rate schedule with effective dates
Counsel guidance on commute travel
Employee acknowledgments of this policy
Quarterly reimbursement audit records

policies.title: Separation of Aides and Notice to CDSS
policies.applies_to: Administrator, supervisors, human resources and payroll staff, schedulers and all affiliated home care aides
policies.purpose: To make sure that when an aide leaves [AGENCY NAME], the Agency notifies CDSS immediately, protects clients and their information, and preserves required records.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] notifies CDSS immediately when it no longer employs an individual as an affiliated home care aide (HSC §1796.43(a)(3)). The notice is made the same business day the separation takes effect, and no later than the end of that day. According to the Agency's research, the notice can be made through the Agency's Guardian account. The Administrator confirms the current method with the CDSS Care Provider Management Branch at 1-888-422-5669 and keeps the confirmed method in the compliance file. The Agency keeps the aide's TB certificate and training logs, and an aide moving to another HCO may take or receive copies so that the next HCO can use them, as the TB screening requirements referenced in HSC §1796.43(a)(2) allow. The Agency retrieves keys, ID badges and all client information on the aide's last day. After the notice is made, the aide no longer has any contact with clients or client information on behalf of the Agency.

definitions.definition: Any end of employment as an affiliated home care aide, whether by resignation, termination, layoff, job abandonment, death or a change to a non-aide position.
An aide employed by the HCO and listed on the Home Care Aide Registry.
The Agency's online account with the CDSS Care Provider Management Branch (Guardian) used to manage aide registry affiliation.
The last day on which the aide is employed by the Agency. The aide has no client contact after separation is effective.

procedures: When an aide resigns, is terminated or is otherwise separated, the supervisor tells the Administrator the same business day. The Administrator records the separation date, reason and method (resignation letter, termination notice or job abandonment).

Where the separation is a termination, the Administrator confirms with counsel when needed that the decision is lawful, documented and consistent with PER-07 and PER-06, and delivers the notice in writing with the effective date.

On the effective date of separation, the Administrator or designee notifies CDSS that the Agency no longer employs the individual as an affiliated home care aide (HSC §1796.43(a)(3)). This is done through the Agency's Guardian account, or by the other method confirmed with the Care Provider Management Branch (1-888-422-5669), on the same business day and no later than the end of that day.

If the Agency learns of a separation after the fact (for example, job abandonment confirmed after missed shifts), the Administrator notifies CDSS on the same day the Agency determines that employment has ended, and documents the date of discovery.
The person who files the notice saves a screenshot or confirmation of the CDSS notice, with the date and time, in the personnel file, and updates the aide roster (RR-03) the same day.

If the aide is separated because of abuse, neglect, exploitation, theft or another reportable event, the Administrator also follows SAF-01, SAF-03 and RR-02 for mandated reports and reports to CDSS, and does not rely on the separation notice alone.

The scheduler removes the aide from all schedules the same day, informs affected clients or families by phone and arranges replacement coverage under SVC-06. The supervisor makes sure no client is left without service.
The aide is removed from timekeeping, EVV and client-record systems, and all passwords, app access and email accounts are disabled by the end of the last day.

On the last day, the supervisor or designee retrieves keys, lockbox codes, ID badges, uniforms or other Agency property, client records, care notes, phone numbers, photos and other client information in any form. Keys and key codes belonging to clients are returned to the client or secured, and lock codes known to the aide are changed if needed.

The Agency never withholds required wages or personal property to force return of items. Payroll issues final wages and any accrued payments on the timeline that counsel has confirmed that California law requires, and pays final mileage reimbursements (PER-10).

If the aide asks, the Agency provides copies of the aide's TB certificate and entry-level and annual training logs so that the next HCO may use them. The Agency keeps the originals, and notes in the personnel file what was released and the date.
The Agency keeps the personnel file, including the TB certificate, training logs, registry clearance records, discipline and separation documents, for the retention period in PER-05 and RR-01.

The Administrator conducts an exit conversation when possible, reminds the aide of continuing confidentiality duties under CR-03 and records any concerns about client safety, which are then followed up under SAF-03 or GOV-04.

Each month, the Administrator compares the Agency's list of active aides in payroll and scheduling with the roster of affiliated aides shown in the Agency's CDSS account. Any aide listed as affiliated who is no longer employed is reported to CDSS that day, and the gap is recorded as a quality finding in GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Files the CDSS notice the same business day; confirms the current notification method with CDSS; decides terminations; monitors monthly roster reconciliation.
Reports separations to the Administrator the same day; retrieves keys, badges and client information; arranges client coverage with the scheduler.
Removes the aide from schedules; contacts affected clients; arranges replacement coverage.
Issues final pay, disables system access, updates the roster and keeps the personnel file with TB and training records.
Returns all Agency property and client information on the last day and keeps client information confidential after separation.

documentation: Resignation letter or termination notice
Separation checklist with property and client-information retrieval
CDSS notice confirmation with date and time
Updated aide roster
Copies of TB certificate and training logs retained in personnel file, with record of any release to the aide
System access disabling record
Final pay and reimbursement records
Monthly roster reconciliation

policies.title: Workers' Compensation and Employee Injury Reporting
policies.applies_to: All affiliated home care aides, office staff, supervisors, the Administrator and the licensee
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] always carries a valid workers' compensation policy covering its affiliated aides, can prove that coverage to CDSS, and handles every work injury promptly, consistently and with documentation.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will maintain, and abide by the terms of, a valid workers' compensation policy covering all affiliated home care aides, as required by HSC §1796.42(b). Proof of coverage on file will include the policy number, the policy dates, and the carrier's name and address, as required for licensure by HSC §1796.37(a)(3). Coverage will never be allowed to lapse. Every aide is an employee (see PER-08) and is covered. Aides must report every work-related injury or illness to their supervisor on the same day it occurs or, if physically unable, as soon as they are able. No aide will be disciplined, retaliated against or discouraged for reporting an injury or filing a claim. [AGENCY NAME] will provide the claim form, notify the insurance carrier, and record the incident under SAF-03. California claim-form and employer-report deadlines have not been verified for this manual. The Administrator will confirm the current deadlines with the carrier and legal counsel, and the carrier's instructions will be followed so that no filing is late.

definitions.definition: Any injury, illness or exposure that an aide or other employee reports as arising out of or occurring in the course of work, including in a client's home, while traveling between clients during work time, or at the office.
The insurance policy that [AGENCY NAME] must maintain covering affiliated aides (HSC §1796.42(b)), identified by policy number, policy dates, and carrier name and address.
The insurance company (or approved administrator) that issues the workers' compensation policy.
The employee claim form for a work injury, which the agency gives the injured employee and which is handled according to the carrier's instructions and California law.

procedures: Before the license application is submitted, the Administrator obtains a workers' compensation policy that covers all affiliated aides and places the certificate and policy in the compliance binder (see GOV-06).

The Administrator records in the compliance binder the policy number, policy effective and expiration dates, and the carrier's name and address, so this information is ready for CDSS under HSC §1796.37(a)(3).

The Administrator calendars the policy expiration date and starts renewal at least 90 days before it. Written confirmation of renewal or replacement must be on file before the current policy ends, so there is no gap in coverage.

The Administrator reviews the policy at least once a year, and whenever the number of aides or payroll changes significantly, to confirm that every aide is covered and the agency is following the policy's terms (for example, payroll reporting and audit requirements).

During orientation (PER-03), each new aide is told how to report a work injury, who to call, and that reporting will not result in retaliation. The aide signs an acknowledgment that goes in the personnel file (PER-05).
The injury-reporting contact information, with the on-call supervisor's phone number [PHONE], is given to every aide in writing and is available 24 hours a day.

When an injury occurs, the aide first gets emergency care if needed. For a serious injury the aide or anyone present calls 911. The aide then tells the on-call supervisor right away, and in all cases the same day.
If the aide is alone with a client and is injured, the supervisor makes sure the client is safe and that coverage is arranged for the rest of the shift, following SVC-06 and SVC-08.
The supervisor records the date, time, location, nature of the injury, body part, witnesses, and what happened, and notifies the Administrator the same day.
The Administrator gives the injured employee the California workers' compensation claim form and a written explanation of how to use it, on the same day as the report or as soon as practical.

The Administrator notifies the workers' compensation carrier of the injury promptly, and follows the carrier's instructions and the deadlines the carrier and counsel have confirmed for the claim form, employer report and any other filing.

The Administrator completes an incident report under SAF-03, noting contributing factors, and the supervisor and Administrator decide on corrective action (for example, retraining or a change to a client's home set-up). If a client or third party was involved, the matter is also handled under SAF-03.

The Administrator keeps in a confidential workers' compensation file (separate from the general personnel file) the claim form, carrier correspondence, work-status notes, and return-to-work documents.

The Administrator keeps in touch with the injured employee and the carrier about work restrictions and return to work, and assigns only work within medical restrictions. Any leave is handled under PER-09.

Quarterly, the Administrator reviews all injuries and near-misses for trends and reports the results to the QA review (GOV-04), including any changes to training (PER-03) or workplace safety practices (SAF-06).
If CDSS asks for proof of workers' compensation coverage, the Administrator provides the policy information from the compliance binder promptly (see RR-02 and RR-03).

responsibilities.duty: Keeps the policy in force without any lapse, maintains proof of coverage, gives claim forms, notifies the carrier on time, confirms current California deadlines with the carrier and counsel, and reviews injury trends.
Receives injury reports at all hours, makes sure the aide and client are safe, documents the report and notifies the Administrator the same day.
Reports every work injury or illness to the supervisor the same day, completes the claim form, and follows medical and return-to-work instructions.
Makes sure the agency has the resources to carry coverage and meet its obligations, and reviews the annual coverage confirmation.

documentation: Workers' compensation policy, certificate, and record of policy number, dates, and carrier name and address
Annual coverage review and renewal confirmations
Signed aide acknowledgment of injury-reporting procedure
Supervisor's injury report notes and SAF-03 incident report
Claim form record and carrier notification record, with dates
Confidential workers' compensation file for each claim
Quarterly injury trend review (QA minutes)

policies.title: Clearance of Office Staff, Schedulers, Supervisors and Volunteers
policies.applies_to: All non-aide staff, volunteers and employees with client contact or access to confidential client information, including schedulers, care supervisors, intake staff and billing staff
policies.purpose: To make sure that no one at [AGENCY NAME], other than a cleared aide, has contact with clients or prospective clients, or access to confidential client information, until the clearance required by California law is complete.
policies.policy: Any staff person, volunteer or employee of [AGENCY NAME] who has contact with clients or prospective clients, or who has access to confidential client information that may pose a risk to client health and safety, must satisfy the requirements of HSC §§1796.23, 1796.24, 1796.25, 1796.26 and 1796.28 BEFORE that contact or access (HSC §1796.43(a)(1)). This applies to schedulers, care supervisors, intake staff, billing staff with access to client data, volunteers, and the Administrator and licensee when they have client contact or data access. Uncleared individuals will not view client files, use the scheduling or billing system with client data, or call, visit or speak with clients or prospective clients. Employment of all of these individuals is conditional on completing clearance and the other conditions in the personnel policies (fingerprint clearance, criminal-conviction statement, and, for aides, TB clearance and registry listing), as stated in the agency's HCS 281 application materials. [AGENCY NAME] may also require criminal record clearance of individuals who are exempt from registration but have client contact (HSC §1796.43(b)). The Act does not state a particular credential for supervisors or schedulers, so [AGENCY NAME] will define qualifications in written job descriptions, as the application requires.

definitions.definition: Completion of the requirements of HSC §§1796.23, 1796.24, 1796.25, 1796.26 and 1796.28, as confirmed and documented by [AGENCY NAME] before client contact or access to confidential client information.
Any in-person, telephone, written or electronic communication with a client, prospective client or the client's family or representative for agency business.
Client names, addresses, health and care information, service plans, schedules, billing and payment data, and any other record described in CR-03 and RR-01.
A person with client contact who is not required to register as an aide, whom the licensee may nevertheless require to obtain criminal record clearance (HSC §1796.43(b)).

procedures: The Administrator maintains a written job description for every position, including schedulers, care supervisors, intake staff and billing staff, as required for the HCO application (HCS 281, Section B2). Each description states that client contact or data access begins only after clearance.

Before extending any offer, the Administrator decides for each position whether the person will have client or prospective-client contact or access to confidential client information. When in doubt, the position is treated as requiring clearance.

Every offer letter states that employment or volunteer service is conditional on completing clearance (including fingerprinting and a criminal-conviction statement) and any other conditions required by the personnel policies. The candidate signs it before starting.

Before the person's first day, the Administrator or designee directs the individual to complete fingerprinting and the clearance steps required by HSC §§1796.23, 1796.24, 1796.25, 1796.26 and 1796.28. For Live Scan and Guardian portal questions, the Care Provider Management Branch can be reached at 1-888-422-5669 or guardian@dss.ca.gov. For other questions, contact the Home Care Services Branch at (877) 424-5778 or HCSB@dss.ca.gov.

The Administrator confirms the current clearance requirements and procedure with CDSS when onboarding the first non-aide employee and whenever CDSS announces a change, and records the confirmation in the compliance binder.
The Administrator records the clearance result and date in a clearance log and places the documentation in the personnel file (PER-05) BEFORE granting any access.

Until clearance is documented, the individual is limited to work with no client contact and no access to client information. The Administrator may not allow them to shadow visits, enter client homes, use the scheduling or billing system with live client data, or attend intake calls.

System access (scheduling, billing, EVV and client records) is granted by the Administrator only after the clearance log shows completion. Access is role-based and limited to the minimum needed for the job (CR-03).

Volunteers are screened and cleared the same way as employees before any client contact or data access. [AGENCY NAME] will not use volunteers for hands-on care and will not have volunteers act as aides.
Where the Administrator requires clearance of an exempt individual with client contact under HSC §1796.43(b), such as a contractor who enters client homes, the same steps and documentation apply.

If clearance is denied, is not obtained, or a new disqualifying issue arises, the Administrator immediately ends the person's client contact and data access, removes system credentials the same day, and addresses employment status with counsel. Discipline and separation follow PER-07 and PER-11.

The Administrator reviews the clearance log quarterly against the staff list and system user list. Any user with client-data access but no clearance record is deactivated the same day, and the finding is reported to the QA review (GOV-04).
Persons who change roles from a no-contact job to one with client contact or data access are treated as new and must be cleared before the change takes effect.

Each cleared individual receives orientation on confidentiality, professional boundaries and mandated reporting (CR-03, PER-07, SAF-01) and signs a confidentiality acknowledgment before access is granted.

responsibilities.duty: Writes job descriptions, determines which positions require clearance, grants system access only after documented clearance, keeps the clearance log, and runs the quarterly access review.
Makes sure no individual without clearance has client contact or data access, and supports corrective action.

responsibilities.role: Scheduler / Intake / Billing Staff and Care Supervisors
responsibilities.duty: Complete clearance before any client contact or data access, and do not contact clients or open client files until notified in writing.
Complete clearance before any client contact or data access and follow confidentiality and boundary rules.

documentation: Job description for every position (HCS 281, Section B2)
Signed conditional offer letter or volunteer agreement
Clearance log with dates and results, and clearance documentation in the personnel file
Record of CDSS confirmation of clearance requirements
System-access grant records and quarterly user-access review
Signed confidentiality acknowledgment
Records of removal of access and corrective action, if any

policies.title: Client Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All staff who create, use, store or release client records; the Administrator and supervisors
federal: 45 CFR 164.530(j) (six-year documentation retention, if a HIPAA covered entity)
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] creates complete, accurate, secure client records, keeps the records that California law requires available for CDSS review, and keeps all records for a defined retention period.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will keep a complete record for every client. The Home Care Services Consumer Protection Act (HSC §1796.10 et seq.) does not set client-record content or a retention period, so the content and retention rules in this policy are adopted by [AGENCY NAME] as its own standard and not as a state mandate. The client record will contain: the intake and assessment; the service plan and every update; the signed service agreement and rights acknowledgment; visit and task notes; medication assistance logs; supervisory visit documentation; incident reports; and complaint and grievance files. [AGENCY NAME] will keep a copy of EACH suspected-abuse report made under HSC §1796.42(e), and those copies will be available to CDSS for review during normal business hours. CDSS may inspect books, records and premises (HSC §1796.52(c)), and [AGENCY NAME] will give access when asked, since refusing access is cause for license revocation. Records will be retained for at least seven (7) years after the client's discharge, as set with legal counsel, and longer if required by law, a legal hold, or counsel's advice. Records are stored securely, with access limited and logged (CR-03).

definitions.definition: All paper and electronic documents about a client's care, services, rights, agreements, incidents and complaints, described in this policy.
A report of suspected or known elder, dependent adult or child abuse made by [AGENCY NAME] or its staff under HSC §1796.42(e), a copy of which must be kept and made available to CDSS.
The minimum time records are kept after the client's discharge. Here, seven (7) years, an agency-adopted period, not a state mandate.
A written instruction from the Administrator or counsel to keep specified records beyond the normal retention period because of an investigation, claim or lawsuit.

procedures: At intake, the intake coordinator opens a record for each client containing the information gathered under SVC-02 and assigns it a client record number.

The record must include: the intake and assessment (SVC-02); the service plan and each update (SVC-03); the signed service agreement and rate and billing disclosure (CR-06); the signed client rights acknowledgment (CR-01); and any grievance or complaint (CR-02).

Aides document every visit the same day: date, start and end times, tasks performed, client condition or changes observed, and any incident. Notes are factual, signed or electronically authenticated, and include the aide's name. Late entries are marked as late.
When medication assistance is provided, the aide completes the medication assistance log for each occurrence as described in SVC-05.
Supervisors document each supervisory visit and the follow-up in the client record (SVC-04) within [NUMBER OF DAYS] days of the visit.
Incident reports (SAF-03) and complaint files (CR-02) are kept with the client record or, if they involve more than one client or an employee, in a cross-referenced confidential file.

When an aide or staff member makes a suspected-abuse report (SAF-01, SAF-02), the Administrator obtains a copy of the report and any confirmation, files it in a separate abuse-report file with the date and the reporter, and cross-references the client record. A copy of EACH report is kept.
The Administrator keeps the abuse-report file in a location where it can be produced promptly during normal business hours if CDSS asks to review it.

Paper records are kept in locked cabinets in a locked office. Electronic records are kept in a password-protected system with role-based access, audit logging and backup. Only cleared staff (PER-13) may access them (CR-03).
Records may be released only as allowed by CR-03, with a valid authorization or as otherwise permitted or required by law. The Administrator logs every release.

When CDSS asks to inspect books, records or premises, staff immediately notify the Administrator. The Administrator gives CDSS access during the inspection and does not refuse, delay or limit access (see GOV-07).

On discharge (SVC-09), the supervisor completes the discharge summary and the Administrator closes the record, records the discharge date and calculates the earliest destruction date (discharge date plus seven years).

Each year the Administrator reviews closed records that have reached the end of the retention period. Before destruction, the Administrator checks for legal holds, pending complaints, investigations and claims, and confirms with counsel if there is any doubt.

Records approved for destruction are shredded or permanently deleted, and the Administrator keeps a destruction log (client record number, date, method and who approved) without keeping the record content.

If a client has a HIPAA-related document (for example, a Notice of Privacy Practices acknowledgment or authorization) and [AGENCY NAME] is a HIPAA covered entity, those HIPAA documents are kept for at least six years under 45 CFR 164.530(j). The seven-year agency standard already covers this.
The Administrator audits a sample of client records every quarter for completeness and timeliness and reports results to the QA review (GOV-04).

policies.title: Required Reports and Notices to the State
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Licensee, Designee and all staff who make or receive reports required by the state
policies.purpose: To list every report and notice [AGENCY NAME] must make to the state, assign responsibility for each, and make sure each is made on time and documented.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will make every report and notice that California law requires of a licensed Home Care Organization. These are: (1) reports of suspected or known elder and dependent adult abuse under WIC §15630 and child abuse under Penal Code §§11164-11174.3, with a copy of each report kept (HSC §1796.42(e)); (2) immediate notice to CDSS when an aide is no longer employed as an affiliated home care aide (HSC §1796.43(a)(3)); (3) a complete aide list and proof of compliance, on CDSS request (HSC §1796.37(a)(5)); (4) license renewal every two years, with the fee postmarked on or before the expiration date (HSC §1796.37(b)); and (5) notice and fees for a change of location ($100) or a change in corporation ($200), per the CDSS fee schedule. [AGENCY NAME] will respond promptly to every CDSS request, because failure to cooperate can lead to withdrawal of an application or expiration or denial of renewal (HSC §1796.37(a)(13)). No periodic statistical or incident reports to CDSS were found in the Act. If CDSS adopts one, the Administrator will add it to this policy.

The CDSS branch that handles Live Scan background checks and online aide registration through the Guardian portal. Phone 1-888-422-5669; email guardian@dss.ca.gov.
An individual registered with CDSS and employed by [AGENCY NAME] to provide non-medical home care.

definitions.term: Change of location / change in corporation
definitions.definition: A change of the HCO's business location, or a change in the corporate or ownership structure of the licensee, each of which carries a fee under the CDSS schedule.

procedures: The Administrator keeps a state reporting calendar in the compliance binder, listing each report and notice in this policy, who is responsible, and the due date or trigger.

Suspected abuse: any staff member who suspects or knows of elder, dependent adult or child abuse follows SAF-01 or SAF-02 and makes the report to the authorities required by WIC §15630 or Penal Code §§11164-11174.3, within the time limits set out in those policies. The reporter notifies the Administrator promptly after reporting, unless the Administrator is the suspected person.

Within one business day after a suspected-abuse report is made, the Administrator obtains a copy of the report and files it in the abuse-report file (RR-01), so a copy of EACH report is kept and available to CDSS during normal business hours. CDSS will cross-report the report it receives to law enforcement and APS or CPS (HSC §1796.52(e)); [AGENCY NAME] does not rely on this and always makes its own report.

Aide separation: on the day an aide stops being employed by [AGENCY NAME] for any reason (resignation, termination, end of assignment), the Administrator notifies CDSS immediately, as required by HSC §1796.43(a)(3), following PER-11, and files proof of the notice (date, time, method and person notified) in the personnel file.

Aide list and proof of compliance: the Administrator keeps the roster under RR-03 current. When CDSS asks for a complete list of affiliated aides and proof that each meets the clearance, training and TB requirements, the Administrator produces it promptly (HSC §1796.37(a)(5)) and records the date and what was sent.

License renewal: the license is renewed every two years. The Administrator calendars the expiration date and prepares the renewal at least 90 days ahead. CDSS mails a fee notice at least 60 days before the renewal date; if it has not arrived by then, the Administrator contacts HCSB at (877) 424-5778 rather than waiting.

The Administrator confirms before renewal that the following are current: insurance (GOV-06), the employee dishonesty bond, workers' compensation (PER-12), and that no fees or civil penalties are outstanding.

The fee for renewal ($5,603 per two years, according to the current CDSS schedule) is mailed so that it is postmarked on or before the license expiration date. The Administrator keeps proof of mailing (postmark, tracking number or receipt) and a copy of the payment.
Change of location: the Administrator notifies CDSS in writing before moving, files the required forms with the $100 fee, and does not operate from the new location until HCSB confirms. See GOV-02.

Change in corporation: before any change in the corporation or ownership of the licensee, the Licensee and Administrator confirm the required forms and the $200 fee with HCSB, file them as CDSS requires, and keep copies. See GOV-01 and GOV-02.
Fee amounts change from time to time. Before each payment, the Administrator checks the CDSS Home Care Services application fee page or calls HCSB to confirm the current amount.

Responding to CDSS: any written or phone request from CDSS is logged the day it arrives with the date, the requester and the due date. The Administrator responds fully and promptly and does not let a request go unanswered, because failure to cooperate can affect licensure (HSC §1796.37(a)(13)). During inspections, follow GOV-07.

Each quarter the Administrator checks the state reporting calendar against the abuse-report file, the separation log and CDSS correspondence, and reports any late or missed filing to the Licensee and the QA review (GOV-04).
Once a year, and whenever the law changes, the Administrator checks with CDSS and legal counsel whether any new periodic report has been required, and updates this policy through GOV-03.

policies.title: Aide Roster, Registry Status and Proof of Compliance on Request
policies.applies_to: Administrator, schedulers and any staff who maintain aide records or assign aides to clients
policies.purpose: To keep a current roster of all affiliated aides that shows registry status and every training and TB requirement, so [AGENCY NAME] can prove compliance to CDSS on request and never schedules an aide whose requirements have lapsed.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will maintain a current roster of all affiliated home care aides showing, for each aide: registry number and status, clearance date, TB exam date and next due date, entry-level training date, and annual training completion. On CDSS request, [AGENCY NAME] will give CDSS a complete list of affiliated aides and proof that each meets HSC §§1796.43, 1796.44 and 1796.45 (HSC §1796.37(a)(5)). The roster will be reviewed monthly. Any TB exam due within 60 days, and any annual training due within 60 days, will be flagged. An aide whose requirement has lapsed will be removed from the schedule until the requirement is met and documented. This follows from the requirements that aides be cleared on the registry before direct client contact (HSC §1796.43(a)), complete entry-level training before providing services, complete annual training each year (HSC §1796.44), and be examined for TB at hire and at least every two years if the result is negative (HSC §1796.45).

definitions.definition: The master record of every affiliated home care aide employed by [AGENCY NAME], with registry, clearance, TB and training data.
Whether the aide is currently listed as cleared on the CDSS Home Care Aide Registry, as verified by the agency.

At least 5 hours before the aide is with a client: 2 hours of orientation on the aide's role and the terms of employment, and 3 hours of safety (basic safety precautions, emergency procedures and infection control) (HSC §1796.44(b)).

At least 5 hours each year, core-competency and population-specific, including clients' rights and safety, daily living needs, reporting, preventing and detecting abuse and neglect, personal hygiene help, and safe transport if transportation is provided (HSC §1796.44(c)).
The licensed practitioner's certificate submitted by the aide after each TB exam, which the agency keeps on file (HSC §1796.45(d)).

procedures: The Administrator creates the aide roster before the first aide is scheduled and keeps it in a secure electronic file, with a printed or exportable copy ready for CDSS.

For every aide, the roster records: full name; registry number and status; date clearance was confirmed; hire date; first client-contact date; TB exam date, result type and next due date; date of entry-level training (with hours); date and hours of each annual training; and status (active, on leave, separated).

Before a new aide's first client contact, the Administrator verifies and enters on the roster the registry clearance (HSC §1796.43(a)), a TB exam within 90 days before hire or within 7 days after (HSC §1796.45(a)), and completed entry-level training (HSC §1796.44). Aides hired with a TB exam in the past 2 years from another HCO are handled under PER-04.

If a TB infection test is positive, the Administrator enters it on the roster only after documenting a chest X-ray and written clearance from a licensed medical professional that the aide has no risk of spreading disease. Once a positive test has been followed by an X-ray, repeat exams are no longer required (HSC §1796.45(b), (c)). Records are kept per PER-04 and PER-05.

The next TB due date is entered as no later than 2 years after the last exam for aides with a negative result (HSC §1796.45(c)), and the practitioner's certificate is filed in the personnel file (HSC §1796.45(d)).

Each aide's annual training due date is set on the anniversary of hire (or another consistent date set by the Administrator), with at least 5 hours of annual training that covers the topics in HSC §1796.44(c). The training record is entered on the roster within 3 business days of completion (PER-03).

On the first business day of each month, the Administrator reviews the whole roster, signs and dates the review, and flags (a) every TB exam due within 60 days, (b) every annual training due within 60 days, and (c) any registry status concern.

For every flagged aide, the Administrator tells the aide and supervisor in writing within 2 business days and sets a deadline before the due date. The aide is helped to schedule the exam or training in time.

The Administrator verifies registry status on the CDSS registry for every aide at least once each month, and whenever the aide's registration renewal date approaches, and records the date and result. Questions are directed to the Care Provider Management Branch at 1-888-422-5669 or HCSB at (877) 424-5778.

If an aide's TB exam, annual training or registry status lapses, the Administrator notifies the scheduler the same day. The scheduler removes the aide from the schedule at once, arranges coverage for affected clients under SVC-06, and does not return the aide to the schedule until the Administrator documents on the roster that the requirement is current.
The Administrator records on the roster each removal and return to work, with dates and the reason.

When CDSS asks for the aide list and proof of compliance, the Administrator produces within the time CDSS gives, or promptly if no time is stated, a complete roster of all affiliated aides together with copies of the proof for each aide (registry clearance, TB certificate, and entry and annual training records) (HSC §1796.37(a)(5)). The Administrator checks the packet for completeness against the personnel files.
The Administrator keeps a copy of each submission to CDSS and logs the request date, due date, date sent, method and who prepared it (RR-02).
When an aide separates, the Administrator marks the aide as separated on the roster on the same day, notifies CDSS under PER-11 and RR-02, and keeps the record per PER-05.

Each quarter, the Administrator reports to the QA review (GOV-04) the number of aides, any lapses, how long each took to correct, and whether any aide was scheduled while out of compliance (which must not occur). Any such event is handled as an incident under SAF-03 and corrected at once.
